articles.title: What Are Solana Privacy Rings? Inside Helius’ Privacy Protocol for Solana - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Solana Privacy Rings are shielded pools that encrypt balances and transfer amounts while keeping execution and settlement on Solana's mainnet.
- The default Ring hides which asset is sent and how much, but wallet addresses stay visible; Custom Rings for institutions add more privacy and compliance controls.
- Rings use zero-knowledge proofs, one of several approaches to blockchain privacy alongside trusted execution environments and fully homomorphic encryption.
Every transaction on Solana is public by default. Anyone can look up a wallet address and see its balance, what it has sent and received, and when. That transparency is useful for verifying the network, but a problem for anyone who doesn't want their finances on display: a business paying salaries, a trader building a position, or an individual who simply doesn't want strangers seeing their savings.
Solana Privacy Rings are designed to fix that, without asking users to leave Solana for a separate privacy network. Developed by Solana infrastructure firm Helius, Rings launched on Solana's mainnet on November 10, 2026.
Today, Solana changes forever
Introducing Solana Privacy Rings - encryption at the speed of Solana
Rings are programmable, onchain environments for encrypting money, markets, and finance - without ever leaving Solana
Now live on mainnet. pic.twitter.com/ezCIUCjcbI
— Helius (@Helius) November 10, 2026
What are Solana Privacy Rings?
Solana Privacy Rings are programmable shielded pools: shared pools on Solana that hold encrypted balances. Users deposit tokens into a Ring, send them privately to other Solana wallets, and withdraw them back to an ordinary public balance whenever they choose, according to the Solana Foundation.
Rings support SOL and other tokens on Solana, including SPL and Token-2022 tokens. Users keep custody of their funds throughout, since every transaction needs the owner's signature.
Crucially, the private balances live on the same network as everything else. Private transactions execute directly on Solana and encrypted data is stored on Solana's ledger, with no separate layer-2 network or sequencer in between. That means private balances sit alongside the same stablecoins, tokenized assets and DeFi liquidity as public ones.
The Solana Foundation describes its approach to privacy as "public by default, private by choice," letting each user or app pick how much privacy it needs.
How do Privacy Rings work?
Helius' developer documentation defines two levels of privacy. Confidentiality encrypts the asset and the amount of a transfer, while anonymity also hides who sent it and who received it. The default Ring is confidential: think of a bank statement where the names on each payment are visible but the amounts are blacked out.
Each private transfer comes with a zero-knowledge proof, a piece of cryptography that lets the network confirm the transfer is valid, for example that the sender actually had the funds, without revealing the numbers involved. Rings use a type of zero-knowledge proof called a Groth16 zk-SNARK, which Helius says can be generated in tens of milliseconds, either by a service provider or on the user's own device. Each private transfer settles in a single Solana transaction.
Users read their own encrypted balances with a viewing key. They can decrypt their balance locally, or let a service provider decrypt it and serve it to them, and they can share a key for a single transaction with an auditor or counterparty without exposing the rest of their history.
Did you know?
Moving funds into a Ring from an ordinary public wallet, or back out again, is visible onchain, including the asset and amount. But users who on-ramp from fiat currency straight into a private balance, through a supported provider, keep the asset and amount hidden from the start, according to Helius.
Default Rings vs. Custom Rings
There are two kinds of Ring:
- Default Ring: live on mainnet and open to anyone. It provides confidentiality: the asset and amount of each transfer are encrypted, but sender and recipient addresses remain public.
- Custom Rings: built for businesses and institutions, each run as its own Solana program with settings chosen by the operator. A Custom Ring can be confidential, or fully anonymous, also hiding who sent and received funds. Operators can add compliance controls such as KYC allowlists, sanctions screening, auditor access and the ability to freeze and recover funds. Custom Rings are in audit and expected to reach mainnet in the coming weeks, according to the Solana Foundation.
Because Custom Rings interoperate with the default Ring, regulated firms can keep their activity confidential from the market while still sharing the same liquidity as everyone else.
What can you do with Privacy Rings?
Private transfers are just the start. Solana programs can hold encrypted balances in private escrows and release them when set conditions are met, opening the way for:
- Private swaps that trade against public liquidity without revealing size or price.
- Private lending, posting collateral without publishing positions.
- Private staking and yield on encrypted balances.
- Conditional payments, such as payroll, vesting or multisig treasury releases.
At launch, Decrypt, mining and staking app ORE and cross-chain service Aurora Intents were using the default Ring, while Backpack, DFlow, Jupiter, Squads and Titan were among the teams working on integrations.
How safe are Privacy Rings?
Helius says the core programs and zero-knowledge circuits have been audited by security firms Certora, OtterSec and ZK Security. Engineers from the Solana Foundation, Blueshift, Zcash and other teams took part in the "trusted setup," the one-off ceremony that generates the parameters the proofs rely on.
The code is open source, published on GitHub under the Apache 2.0 license, so anyone can inspect how it works.
Formal verification, a mathematical check that the circuits behave exactly as intended, is still underway and expected to finish by the end of 2026. Solana's own documentation currently describes Rings as being in beta.
Privacy tools also come with compliance questions. The launch came days after another Solana privacy protocol, Privacy Cash, temporarily paused deposits in light of the October 2026 Binance hack, saying it wanted to "make sure bad actors can't use our product" while it strengthened its wallet screening. Stolen funds from the hack had been deposited into its pools, according to blockchain analytics firm Elliptic. The default Ring leaves addresses, deposits and withdrawals visible, and Helius works with blockchain analytics firms Range, Chainalysis and Elliptic on wallet screening.
How do Privacy Rings compare with other privacy tech?
Rings are one of three privacy tools Solana itself offers. Its documentation also lists Confidential Balances, a Token-2022 extension that encrypts token balances and transfer amounts while keeping accounts public, and Private Channels, private execution environments run by an institution.
Across the wider industry, blockchain privacy tends to rely on four broad families of technology:
- 📝 Zero-knowledge proofs (zk-SNARKs): These let one party prove a statement is true without revealing the underlying data. Privacy coin Zcash uses zk-SNARKs to power its shielded transactions, as Decrypt's guide explains. Privacy Rings belong to this family, using compact Groth16 proofs, but bring shielded pools to Solana instead of a dedicated privacy chain.
- ⭕ Ring signatures: Used by privacy coin Monero, a ring signature can be produced by any member of a group of keyholders, without revealing which one actually signed. Monero mixes a user's real transaction output with others pulled from the blockchain to form a "ring" of possible signers, so outside observers can't tell which one is real, according to the Monero Project's Moneropedia. Despite the similar name, Solana Privacy Rings don't use ring signatures.
- 📱 Trusted execution environments (TEEs): Rather than cryptography alone, TEEs use secure areas of a computer's hardware, sometimes called enclaves, to process private data out of view of the rest of the system—the same sort of hardware used to store biometric data on smartphones. They're efficient and can run existing code, but require trusting the chip's manufacturer, and they have been vulnerable to side-channel attacks, according to a primer from venture firm a16z.
- 🧮 Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE): FHE lets computers perform calculations directly on encrypted data without ever decrypting it, which makes it possible to run smart contracts on private inputs. The technique is powerful but computationally heavy, making it slower and more costly than other approaches for now.
In short, Privacy Rings take the zero-knowledge route: they rely on mathematics rather than trusted hardware, and they hide amounts rather than performing private computation in the way FHE aims to. Their main distinguishing feature is where they run, on Solana's mainnet itself, rather than on a separate privacy network.
Disclosure
Decrypt has partnered with Helius to offer confidential transfers in the Decrypt Money Account using Solana Privacy Rings.

articles.title: Barclays Boosts IBIT Stake 48% Ahead of 13F Filing Deadline
articles.text:
Barclays boosts BlackRock Bitcoin ETF stake 48% as banks expand holdings
Barclays reported a $187 million stake as of Sept. 30, while Citigroup disclosed a new $119 million position in Fidelity’s Bitcoin ETF.
Barclays reported holding 3.94 million shares in BlackRock’s spot Bitcoin exchange-traded fund (ETF) at the end of the third quarter, up 48% from the previous quarter.
The position in the iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT) was worth about $187 million on Sept. 30, up from $88.5 million for 2.66 million shares on June 30, according to Barclays’ Friday Form 13F filing.
“Early readings suggest longer-term holders make up a growing share of the spot bitcoin ETF investor base,” Bitwise analyst Camran Khosravi told Cointelegraph, pointing to increased bank exposure, including at Citigroup.
Citigroup reported a new position worth about $119 million in the Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC). Its reported IBIT holdings also rose 50% to about 521,000 shares, from 347,000 at the end of June.
The filings offer an early indication of changing institutional Bitcoin ETF ownership, with more major banks and hedge funds yet to disclose their third-quarter positions. Institutional investment managers have until Monday to file their third-quarter holdings reports.
Banks gain ground among Bitcoin ETF holders
Banks accounted for $258 million, or 4.9%, of reported spot Bitcoin ETF holdings among early third-quarter filers, up from $107 million, or 3.2%, in Q2, according to Bitwise data shared with Cointelegraph.
Investment advisers remained the largest holders, accounting for $3.5 billion, or 66.6%, of reported positions, up from $2.2 billion in the previous quarter. Bitwise compared holdings across the two quarters for the 1,389 institutions that had filed their third-quarter reports by Friday. The value of their combined spot Bitcoin ETF holdings rose to $5.25 billion from $3.35 billion.
Khosravi said financial advisers at major banks and wealth platforms can now recommend Bitcoin ETFs to clients, a development he expects to become increasingly visible in institutional filings over the coming quarters.
Related: Global banks commit $270M to stablecoin venture targeting 2027 launch
The figures remain preliminary, with major holders including JPMorgan, Wells Fargo and hedge funds Millennium and Schonfeld yet to report their positions ahead of the upcoming deadline.
Price gains lift the value of Bitcoin ETF holdings
Rising Bitcoin ETF valuations do not necessarily reflect fresh institutional buying, according to Jonatan Randin, senior market analyst at PrimeXBT.
“It’s important to look at the holdings in shares and not just the increase in dollar amount,” Randin told Cointelegraph, noting that IBIT gained about 41% in price in Q3.
Separately, an October CoinShares survey found that diversification accounted for 40% of responses on why investors held digital assets, compared with less than 9% for speculation.
Randin cautioned that the filings capture holdings as of Sept. 30, before Bitcoin’s subsequent decline and outflows from spot ETFs. US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded about $6.34 billion in net inflows during the third quarter, followed by roughly $2.1 billion in net outflows in Q4 through Tuesday, according to SoSoValue data.

articles.title: Kraken’s xStocks Launches 200+ Tokenized UK, EU Stocks
articles.text:
Kraken parent adds over 200 tokenized UK and EU stocks to xStocks
The expansion adds more than 200 tokenized UK and EU equities, including all 40 companies in Germany’s DAX index, as xStocks plans further expansion into Hong Kong.
Kraken parent Payward’s xStocks platform added tokenized versions of more than 200 stocks listed in the United Kingdom and European Union.
Payward said Wednesday that eligible users can trade the new tokens on Kraken and participating xStocks Alliance platforms. The tokens remain unavailable to investors in the UK.
The expansion includes tokenized shares of all 40 companies in Germany’s benchmark DAX index, including SAP, Siemens, Allianz and Deutsche Telekom. According to a separate Wednesday announcement from Deutsche Börse, the tokens are available for trading on its affiliated 360X platform, with 24/7 trading supported on select venues.
Payward said the latest expansion brings xStocks’ offering to more than 1,500 tokenized assets. The company reported more than $45 billion in cumulative transaction volume and over 550,000 unique holders.
According to Payward, the new tokens are backed one-to-one by shares held with a regulated custodian. Kraken’s risk disclosure says xStocks tokens give holders exposure to the shares’ performance without voting rights or legal claims to the underlying stock.
Token Terminal data put xStocks’ market capitalization at $1.1 billion, about 22% of the $4.9 billion in tokenized stocks the firm tracks. xStocks ranked third, behind Binance bStocks at $1.5 billion and Ondo Finance at $1.4 billion.
Payward said it plans to add hundreds of Hong Kong-listed equities in the coming weeks.
Related: Kraken launches xChange engine to power tokenized stock trading

articles.title: A High-Severity Bug Could Have Stalled Bitcoin Mining—Bitcoin Core Has a Fix - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Bitcoin Core disclosed three now-patched security flaws in the software running most of the network’s nodes, covering denial-of-service and privacy issues rather than anything enabling coin theft or forgery.
- The most serious could corrupt a node’s mempool during a chain reorganization, halting a miner’s ability to create block templates until restarted.
- None reached Bitcoin Core’s “critical” tier, and no exploitation was reported.
Bitcoin Core developers have disclosed three security vulnerabilities in the software that runs most of the Bitcoin network, including one high-severity bug that could disrupt mining, all of which have since been fixed.
The flaws, detailed in a batch of security advisories, span denial-of-service and privacy issues rather than anything that would let an attacker steal coins or forge Bitcoin.
Bitcoin Core, the reference software operating the majority of the network’s nodes, classifies vulnerabilities into four tiers, from “low” to “critical,” and these fell into the middle of that range.
The most serious, tracked as CVE-2025-62861, concerns block template creation, the process miners rely on to assemble new blocks.
According to the advisory, a chain reorganization could trigger an erroneous eviction of certain transactions, corrupting a node’s mempool, its waiting room for unconfirmed transactions, so that an affected node could no longer build block templates until it was restarted. For a miner, that means a halt to the very work that earns block rewards.
A second flaw, CVE-2025-62859, could let a peer stall a node’s block processing by announcing a compact block with a manipulated witness, a form of transaction malleation.
The third, CVE-2025-62860, was a privacy and security issue in which inbound connections over the Tor anonymity network were wrongly granted “whitelist” permissions, lifting various denial-of-service and privacy protections on affected nodes.
None of the three rises to the “critical” level Bitcoin Core reserves for bugs that threaten coin theft at the protocol level, unauthorized coin creation or permanent network-wide chain splits. The developers did not report any evidence the flaws were exploited.
The disclosures come amid a broader reckoning over how quickly Bitcoin’s defenders can keep pace with a shifting threat landscape.
Bitcoin Core recently rewrote its security policy to account for AI, adding a category for “easily discoverable” vulnerabilities that can be surfaced through a simple AI prompt, which it now patches and discloses immediately rather than holding under a long embargo.
That shift reflects mounting concern that large language models have lowered the bar for finding flaws, a worry underscored by the volunteer “Bitcoin Red Team,” which has been racing to uncover AI-discoverable bugs across the ecosystem before attackers can exploit them.
The fixes themselves shipped earlier, with the advisories following under Bitcoin Core’s disclosure timeline. Node operators are generally urged to run the latest software to stay protected.

articles.title: Bitcoin Short-Term Holders Send BTC to Exchanges as They Slip Into Net Loss
articles.text:
Bitcoin short-term holders send 47K BTC to exchanges at a loss
Bitcoin fell to an 11-week low of $72,670 after slipping below short-term holders’ average cost basis of about $75,700, according to CryptoQuant.
Bitcoin (BTC) short-term holders sent more than 47,000 BTC to exchanges on Tuesday as Bitcoin fell to an 11-week low, with the coins worth less than their purchase price.
Key points:
- Short-term holders moved 47,025 BTC to exchanges while the coins were worth less than their acquisition price.
- The 24-hour total was the third-highest since July, according to CryptoQuant.
- CryptoQuant’s Julio Moreno said a sustained break below $73,000 and a failed rebound above that level would strengthen the case that Bitcoin’s broader downtrend was continuing.
Short-term holders’ underwater exchange inflows rank third since July
Data from onchain analytics platform CryptoQuant showed short-term holders sent 47,025 BTC carrying unrealized losses to exchanges in the 24 hours to midnight UTC at the start of Wednesday.
The tally was among the largest 24-hour totals in the four months of data tracked by CryptoQuant and came as Bitcoin dropped to $72,670, its lowest level since Aug. 20.
The short-term holder metric tracks Bitcoin held for up to 155 days. Short-term holders are generally considered more likely to sell when prices fall, even at a loss.
“On November 10, profitable transfers stood near 1,700 BTC, meaning approximately 27 BTC arrived at a loss for every 1 BTC transferred at a profit,” CryptoQuant said.
The largest 24-hour inflows of BTC carrying unrealized losses since late July occurred on Oct. 8, hours after Bitcoin fell back to $80,000. Rolling 24-hour inflows peaked at 50,500 BTC.
Short-term holders’ exchange inflows of BTC carrying unrealized losses. Source: CryptoQuant
CryptoQuant analyst flags $73,000 as Bitcoin tests August lows
Cointelegraph previously reported that short-term holders’ average cost basis was around $75,700.
Related: Stock ETF buyers pounce on dip as Bitcoin funds bleed $1.6 billion
Short-term holders moved into an aggregate unrealized profit on Aug. 20 as Bitcoin rebounded toward $80,000. They slipped back into an aggregate unrealized loss on Friday.
STH cost basis vs. BTC/USD. Source: CryptoQuant
CryptoQuant head of research Julio Moreno said Bitcoin could still be in the downtrend that began in November 2025.
“If rallies keep stalling near the cohort’s cost basis and net unrealized losses deepen, the August rebound starts to look like a pause in the broader downtrend,” he wrote on Monday.
“A sustained break below $73,000 followed by a failed retest from below would strengthen the case for bear-market continuation.”
STH-NUPL vs. BTC/USD. Source: CryptoQuant
CryptoQuant’s net unrealized profit/loss (NUPL) metric showed that short-term holders reached their highest level of unrealized profitability since November 2025 as Bitcoin climbed to $87,200 in September.

articles.title: OKX-ICE Tokenized Stock Venue Sets Launch, Turning to Crypto Companies After Big Tech Opts Out - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- OKXICE, the joint venture between OKX and NYSE owner ICE, will open its tokenized securities venue on Nov. 23 with more than 70 assets, including 59 Direxion ETFs.
- Launch issuers include Coinbase, Circle, Robinhood and Strategy, crypto-friendly companies that didn’t appear among the 67 objectors as of Nov. 5.
- Securitize will provide the tokenization, with each token backed one-for-one by a real share, and access is limited to eligible U.S. OKX customers.
After weeks of rejections from corporate America, OKX and ICE’s tokenized stock venue has found its launch lineup: crypto’s own public companies.
OKXICE said Wednesday that its Tokenized Securities Venue will open Nov. 23, letting eligible U.S. customers trade tokenized securities around the clock in the OKX app.
More than 70 assets are expected to be listed, including securities from Coinbase, Circle, Robinhood, Strategy, BitGo, Securitize and Better.com, plus 59 ETFs from Direxion. Strategy will also list its preferred stocks.
That’s a very different roster from the one the venue started with. As of its Nov. 5 notice, 67 companies, including every member of the “Magnificent Seven” tech giants, had objected to having their shares traded on the platform. Coinbase, Robinhood and Strategy were notably absent from that list, and all three are now among the venue’s launch issuers.
“The SEC has created a real opening for American markets to lead the next era of finance,” said former New York Gov. Andrew Cuomo, who co-chairs OKXICE, a joint venture between OKX and NYSE owner Intercontinental Exchange.
Securitize will provide the tokenization infrastructure. Each token represents an entitlement backed one-for-one by a real U.S. share, carrying dividends, voting rights and other shareholder benefits, according to the announcement.
Trading will run through automated market maker pools built on Uniswap v4 on X Layer, OKX’s Ethereum layer-2 network, and customers will hold their tokens in self-custodial wallets.
Strategy CEO Phong Le called tokenization on the venue “a natural next step” for the company’s preferred stocks, such as STRC.
Access is limited to eligible U.S.-based OKX customers who activate a CeDeFi Wallet, pass identity verification and complete onboarding with OKXICE. The venue operates under the SEC’s innovation exemption, which the agency unveiled in September after the Clarity Act failed to advance in the Senate. Under the exemption, companies can keep third-party tokenized versions of their stock off a given venue by objecting within 30 days.
The launch caps a busy stretch for Wall Street tokenization. DTCC’s new tokenization service, which runs partly on the Canton Network, went live in late October, and Morgan Stanley said it was among the first banks to use it.

articles.title: Decrypt Becomes First News Publisher to Offer Perps Trading, Powered by Solana's Phoenix - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Read it. Trade it. Now with perps. Decrypt is integrating perpetual futures, powered by Solana exchange Phoenix, as the first media platform to let readers go long or short on the news.
- Crypto, stocks and commodities, 24/7. Phoenix offers round-the-clock perps on crypto, U.S. stocks, gold and pre-IPO companies, all funded from a single Decrypt Money Account balance.
- From information to execution. Perps join prediction markets, swaps and Earn as Decrypt builds The Information Exchange, where news, data and markets come together in one place.
What happens when the place you read the news becomes the place you act on it?
The news that moves markets and the tools to trade them have long lived in separate places. Decrypt is bringing them together.
Decrypt is integrating perpetual futures trading, powered by Phoenix, a fully onchain perpetuals exchange on Solana, making it the first media platform to offer perps trading directly alongside its journalism.
Readers will be able to take long or short positions on crypto, stocks and commodities from the same place they follow the news that moves them, without switching apps, connecting external wallets or moving funds between platforms.
"Information influences decisions, shapes opinions and moves markets," said Ilan Hazan, co-founder and COO of Decrypt. "A reader might discover an opportunity through a publication, develop a view and then leave to act on it somewhere else. The publisher monetizes the impression, while someone else monetizes the transaction. It means the publisher captures only a small part of the economic activity that its information and distribution generates."
Rather than treating media and financial products as separate businesses, he said, Decrypt is bringing them together. "We're allowing readers to go from understanding what's happening in the markets to taking a position, without leaving Decrypt.”
"Partnering with Decrypt closes the gap between reading the news and acting on it," said Kabir Sethi, Head of Business Development at Phoenix. "With over 100 Phoenix perpetuals markets built directly into Decrypt, readers can take in a story, form a view, and trade it in the same place. We are excited to help play a part in transforming Decrypt into a true information exchange."
Perpetual futures, or perps, are contracts that let traders bet on an asset's price rising or falling without an expiry date, typically using leverage. Leverage magnifies both gains and losses, and positions can be liquidated quickly when markets move against them.
Phoenix offers markets in crypto, U.S. stocks, gold and pre-IPO companies around the clock, with up to 40x leverage and low fees, according to its website. It is developed by Ellipsis Labs, a team that has built exclusively on Solana and whose CEO, Eugene Chen, has described perps as having "crazy product market fit."
"These are very, very strong, high revenue businesses, probably some of the best in the industry," Chen said of perps exchanges in a podcast interview with Blockworks' Lightspeed earlier this year. Phoenix routes each trade at the moment it lands onchain, splitting it between its order book and market makers "based on what's going to give you the best price," he explained.
One account, every market
Perps trading runs through the Decrypt Money Account, a single self-custodial account on Solana designed to work without seed phrases, gas fees or bridging.
One balance now funds it all: prediction markets on Decrypt Predict, Jupiter-powered token swaps, Earn and, now, perpetual futures. Users can also send funds privately, after Decrypt added confidential transfers through Solana infrastructure firm Helius.
Imagine reading about a public company's earnings and taking a position on its stock, at any hour. Or following a breaking story about Bitcoin and going long or short in the same moment.
From information to execution, in one place.
The Information Exchange
Announced in September, The Information Exchange is Decrypt's vision for the next generation of financial media: a single destination bringing together news, intelligence, market data, probabilities, direct financial participation—with perps forming the latest building block in that infrastructure.
News moves markets. Now readers can move with it.

Perpetual futures are leveraged products and carry a high risk of loss. Availability may vary by region.

articles.title: Bitget Wallet Reports Sevenfold Surge in Crypto Phishing Alerts
articles.text:
Bitget Wallet reports sevenfold jump in crypto phishing risk alerts
The wallet flagged about 37,000 signing requests a week for phishing in Q3 and said better monitoring likely contributed to the increase.
Crypto wallet provider Bitget Wallet said Wednesday it was expanding AI-assisted threat detection after its weekly average of signing requests flagged for potential phishing rose 7.4-fold in the third quarter of 2026.
The wallet flagged about 37,000 such requests per week in Q3, up from 5,000 in Q2, according to Bitget Wallet chief operating officer Alvin Kan.
“The increase likely reflects both greater threat activity and improved detection capabilities, although the data does not allow us to quantify each factor’s contribution,” Kan told Cointelegraph.
The wallet introduced AI-assisted risk detection in Q2, he added.
Kan said that the tally counted flagged signing interactions, not unique attacks or confirmed financial losses.
Bitget Wallet said its expanded AI checks examine website code and domain registration details for signs of fraud. The wallet also simulates transactions to spot hidden permissions before users sign.
Bitget Wallet also said AI helped identify 90% of newly blocked risky domains in October, compared with 36% in Q2. Nearly 70% of domains its AI flagged that month had no matching alerts in the external threat feeds it checked.
The findings come amid continued phishing threats targeting crypto users. In July, a trader lost nearly $1 million after signing a malicious Ethereum token approval.

articles.title: Morning Minute: What Anthropic’s $1.4 Trillion IPO Means for Crypto - Decrypt
articles.text:
Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.
GM!
Today’s top news:
- Crypto majors rebound after Tuesday selloff; BTC at $74k
- Anthropic shares plans to IPO on Nov 19th at $1T mc
- Consortium of big banks commit $270M to build stablecoin competitor
- Grayscale pledges $1M to Zcash nonprofits, including WSJ front page ad
- CFTC warns Kalshi over potential enforcement charges tied to new contracts
💵 What Anthropic’s $1.4 Trillion IPO Means for Crypto
Several key new details for Anthropic’s pending IPO were released on Tuesday. The IPO price range was set at $70 to $78 a share, selling 825 million Class A shares to raise about $64.4 billion (at the top of the range). Pricing is expected November 18, with trading starting November 19 on Nasdaq under ANT. Roughly 20% of the deal is set aside for retail, which is about double what a book this size usually gives individual investors.
At the range, Anthropic is worth $916 billion to $1.02 trillion on basic shares, or up to $1.405 trillion fully diluted. In September the company was reportedly eyeing $2 trillion. The Wall Street Journal says major investors now see it landing closer to $1 trillion after last week’s AI selloff. That’s a 30% markdown in two months, and the order book is only reported as covered, not oversubscribed.
Notably on Hyperliquid, ANT is trading at $1.8T with $100M in daily trading volume and $200M in open interest (a big enough market to provide some signal). So perhaps traders are a bit more bullish on ANT price action than Wall Street.
Alongside the IPO sits a $26 billion private placement of non-voting Class N stock, bought at the IPO price by seven of Anthropic’s own compute suppliers. Google and Nvidia take about $10 billion each, AMD $2.5 billion, Broadcom, Micron and Microsoft about $1 billion apiece, TSMC $500 million. Those shares carry no lock-up. Combined with the IPO, Anthropic walks away with roughly $84.6 billion for general corporate purposes, mostly compute.
Regarding financials, Anthropic just reported revenue of $33.2 billion through nine months against $2.5 billion a year earlier and a $1.26 billion operating loss. It reported a $104 billion net loss, almost all of it a non-cash charge on convertible notes. And $900.9 billion in committed spending, with $70.7 billion due inside twelve months.
So what does it mean for crypto?
The liquidity drain thesis has been circulating since April, when CoinDesk laid out the case that mega-IPOs pull speculative money from the same pool that funds crypto. Retail allocations are the mechanism. A dollar earmarked for an IPO ticket is a dollar not in Bitcoin or memecoins.
We already ran this experiment. SpaceX listed June 12 at more than $2 trillion. Bitcoin fell 29% going into it, bottomed at $58,500 on June 30, and then rose 37% off that low. But notably, the Bitcoin bottom was effectively in on June 5 at $59k, a full week ahead of the SPCX IPO.
So the question is not whether an IPO pulls money out. It’s whether that already happened. Bitcoin fell roughly 15% from its early-October high through a $6.3 billion exchange hack, an AI capex selloff and a Democratic sweep.
Two things make this deal smaller than it looks for crypto. The retail slice is roughly $12.9 billion against SpaceX’s $22 billion, about 59% as much. And the $26 billion private placement never touches public market liquidity at all, because it comes from Anthropic’s vendors, who then get paid back in compute contracts.
Thus, if the SpaceX pattern repeats, and with the ~60% factor, we could expect BTC to drop another 5% or so into the Anthropic IPO (notably, that’s right where the 200-week moving average is). And we would expect the effective bottom to be in sometime in the next 1-2 days.
The good news is, the pain is mostly behind us, in that scenario. We will find out soon enough if IPO history repeats itself for crypto…

articles.title: Bitmine Reports $6.3B Annual Net Loss as Ether Falls
articles.text:
Bitmine posts $6.3B net loss for fiscal 2026 as Ether prices slide
Bitmine booked $6.2 billion in unrealized losses on digital assets. It held 6.07 million ETH on Sunday, or 4.97% of Ether’s supply.
Bitmine Immersion Technologies reported a $6.3 billion net loss for the fiscal year ended Aug. 31, driven largely by falling Ether (ETH) prices.
The company recorded a $6.2 billion unrealized loss on its digital assets, according to the Form 10-K it filed Tuesday. Bitmine posted a $348.6 million net profit the previous fiscal year.
Bitmine reported $15.4 billion in total assets and $33.7 million in liabilities at fiscal year-end. It held 5.9 million Ether worth $14.6 billion. Assets also included $545 million in cash and cash equivalents, 211 Bitcoin (BTC) valued at $16.6 million, $186 million in Beast Industries shares and $77 million in Eightco Holdings shares.
Bitmine’s revenue totaled $124.8 million, above the $119.8 million average analyst estimate listed by Yahoo Finance. Staking and validation accounted for $121.4 million, or 97% of revenue.
Bitmine shares closed 2.8% lower at $18.08 on Tuesday, bringing their year-to-date decline to 33%, according to Yahoo Finance. The company filed the 10-K after the market closed.
Bitmine, the largest corporate Ether holder, said in a Monday update that its holdings grew to 6.07 million ETH, or 4.97% of the supply. It estimated $309 million in annualized rewards on the 5.23 million ETH it had staked.
During a keynote at Token2049 in Singapore on Oct. 7, Bitmine Chairman Tom Lee called 5% of Ether’s supply a “hard cap” for the company’s holdings.

articles.title: Kraken Parent Payward Brings 200 UK and EU Stocks Onchain as xStocks - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Payward has tokenized more than 200 of the most actively traded UK and EU-listed stocks as xStocks, its biggest expansion beyond U.S. equities to date.
- The tokens, backed 1:1 by the underlying shares, are available on Kraken and partner platforms in more than 110 markets, but not to UK investors.
- Hong Kong-listed stocks are next, while the London Stock Exchange plans to list xStocks on its 24-hour LSE 24 venue in 2027, subject to approval.
Payward, the parent company of crypto exchange Kraken, has tokenized more than 200 UK and European stocks through its xStocks platform, it announced on Wednesday.
The first batch covers some of the most actively traded companies listed in the UK and the European Union, with more to be added on a rolling basis. Like other xStocks, each token is backed 1:1 by the underlying share, which is bought and held by a regulated custodian for as long as the token trades, according to Payward.
Payward's @xStocksFi is expanding beyond US tokenized equities.
In partnership with @GTNglobal, more than 200 of the UK and EU’s largest equities are now tokenized by xStocks, including HSBC, Shell, LVMH and Airbus.
The first international launch, with more markets to follow.…
— Payward (@Payward) November 11, 2026
The tokens are available to trade on Kraken and through other platforms in the xStocks Alliance, and on blockchains where xStocks already trade, including Solana, Ethereum and TON. They are offered in more than 110 markets, but remain unavailable to investors in the UK.
"A portfolio should not have borders or trading hours," said Mark Greenberg, Payward's chief commercial officer. "Tokenizing every other international market is the next step."
The launch takes xStocks past 1,500 tokenized stocks, ETFs and IPOs. The platform holds more than $1.1 billion in assets, has processed over $45 billion in total transaction volume, and has more than 550,000 holders, Payward said.
The road to London
The new tokens are the first delivered under Payward's partnership with GTN, a brokerage infrastructure firm that handles execution and custody of the underlying shares. When the two partnered in July, Payward said it planned to start with Hong Kong-listed stocks; hundreds of Hong Kong listings will now follow in the coming weeks, the company said.
The expansion also delivers on part of Payward's partnership with the London Stock Exchange, announced in September, under which Payward agreed to tokenize the 100 largest London-listed companies. Subject to regulatory approval, the exchange intends to list xStocks and begin trading them on LSE 24, its planned near-24-hour trading venue, in 2027.
Payward has been drawing interest from traditional exchanges. Nasdaq agreed to invest $100 million in the company at a $21 billion valuation in September, building on a March partnership to bring tokenized stocks to market in 2027, while Deutsche Börse bought a $200 million stake in April.
The company has also been expanding through acquisitions, agreeing to buy derivatives exchange Bitnomial for $550 million and Lithuania's Saldo Bank as part of a push into the EU.

articles.title: ECB Warns Legislative Delays Could Postpone Digital Euro Launch
articles.text:
ECB warns legislative delays could postpone digital euro launch
ECB Executive Board member Piero Cipollone warned EU lawmakers that delays in finalizing digital euro legislation could push back its potential 2029 rollout.
European Central Bank (ECB) Executive Board member Piero Cipollone called for European Union negotiators to reach a deal on digital euro legislation by year-end to keep a possible 2029 launch on track.
Speaking at the European Parliament’s Committee on Economic and Monetary Affairs on Tuesday, Cipollone said adoption of the regulation, part of the EU’s Single Currency Package, would give the ECB the legal certainty it needs to complete preparations.
“A delay in adoption could instead postpone the introduction of the digital euro,” Cipollone said, warning that a later launch could deepen Europe’s dependence on foreign payment providers and make it harder for European companies to compete.
The ECB aims to be ready for a potential first issuance in 2029 if the EU adopts the regulation this year. Its Governing Council will decide whether and when to issue the digital euro after the legislation passes.
The European Parliament’s economic affairs committee approved its position on the digital euro legislation in June in a 43–14 vote. Parliament adopted its negotiating position in July, clearing the way for talks with EU member states.
The ECB is preparing a 12-month pilot set to begin in the second half of 2027. Payment providers and selected merchants will test a beta version of the digital euro.
The warning comes as the ECB prepares for a leadership change. President Christine Lagarde announced in October that she would step down on Feb. 7, 2027, ahead of the planned pilot.
Related: ECB President Christine Lagarde to step down in February 2027

articles.title: Novig loses court shield, and New York gambling laws strike back
articles.text:
Quick Take
- A federal judge denied Novig preliminary protection from New York gambling laws in a Nov. 10 ruling.
- The court said state gambling rules could apply even if Novig's sports contracts qualified as federal swaps.
- The order leaves its federal exchange designation intact and addresses interim relief.
Sports event-contract exchange Novig was denied preliminary protection from New York's gambling laws on Nov. 10, with a federal judge concluding that the sports contracts at issue remained subject to state rules despite its federal exchange designation.
The opinion goes beyond whether those contracts qualify as swaps under federal commodities law. The judge reasoned that even assuming they do, New York could still apply its gambling rules to the betting activity.
Novig filed a notice of appeal to the US Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit that same day, challenging the denial of its preliminary-injunction request.
The dispute separates permission to operate a federally designated exchange from protection against state sports-betting requirements.
According to the opinion, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) designated Novig as a contract market on June 16, and Novig announced availability of New York sports contracts on Aug. 4.
Two grounds for denying protection
At this preliminary stage, US District Judge McMahon first concluded that Novig's sports contracts fell outside the Commodity Exchange Act's definition of swaps.
The judge accepted that sporting outcomes could qualify as events or contingencies. Applying her contextual reading of the statute, she found that Novig's contracts lacked the required inherent financial, economic or commercial connection.
Federal designation of the exchange left the court to decide the classification of the particular contracts.
The opinion also considered the alternative assumption that the contracts are swaps.
McMahon reasoned that even then, the CFTC's exclusive jurisdiction left room for some state rules affecting an exchange. She distinguished federal control over the licensing and operation of designated contract markets from the incidental application of New York gambling laws to betting conducted on them.
That creates a second obstacle for Novig's federal-shield argument, which is that establishing swap status alone would leave the opinion's separate reasoning about the survival of state gambling law to be addressed.
The judge also rejected Novig's argument that complying with both federal and state law was impossible. She pointed to pursuing state licensing and using geographic controls while operating the exchange. The court described those steps as possible routes to compliance.
A similar alternative reasoning was used in the Sixth Circuit's Kalshi litigation. The new development is its application to Novig's request for protection against New York officials.
The Nov. 10 order denies interim relief and leaves Novig's federal exchange designation in place. Its disposition is limited to the preliminary-injunction motion, while a nationwide ban, a nationwide shutdown directive, and a final merits judgment all fall outside its scope.

articles.title: Nvidia Sheds $430B in Two Days as Jensen Huang Faces Calls to Resign - Decrypt
articles.text:
Nvidia has lost about $430 billion in market value in two days, as pressure grows in Washington over CEO Jensen Huang's ties to a businesswoman U.S. intelligence reportedly concluded was a Chinese spy.
Nvidia shares closed down 5.5% at $168.89 on Tuesday, following a 4.3% drop on Monday, according to Yahoo! Finance. That leaves the stock down about 9.5% since Friday's close, wiping out roughly $430 billion in market value, according to Yahoo! Finance data. The sell-off, which saw shares slide as much as 8% on Monday, has wiped out all of Nvidia's gains for 2026. The shares were up 3.8% at $175.23 in premarket trading early on Wednesday.
The independent members of Nvidia's board have retained Joon Kim, a former acting U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of New York, and his firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to carry out the investigation it announced on Sunday, the company said on Tuesday.
A new statement from the independent members of the NVIDIA Board: https://t.co/uSFDhiohG8
— NVIDIA Newsroom (@nvidianewsroom) November 10, 2026
Calls for Huang to go
Sen. Kevin Cramer, a North Dakota Republican on the Senate Banking Committee, called on Huang to step down, telling Politico late Tuesday that the risk of extortion was too great. "The potential for extortion is so tremendous that something as sensitive as Nvidia chips, I just think he's got to go," Cramer said, adding that the board's internal investigation was "fine, but not nearly enough."
Hours earlier, former National Economic Council director Larry Kudlow had urged Huang to resign on his Fox Business show. "Step down, Mr. Huang, right now," Kudlow said, adding that he was "not here to indict" Huang but that he should step aside while the investigations take place.
Cramer's committee has jurisdiction over bills that would curb Nvidia chip sales to China, including the AI Overwatch Act and the Chip Security Act, which are being considered for inclusion in the annual defense spending bill, Politico reported.
Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer, meanwhile, accused President Donald Trump of failing to act after being briefed on the relationship. "What a dereliction of duty," Schumer said on the Senate floor on Tuesday, according to CNBC. "He's supposed to protect America, not China, not his friends."
Rep. John Moolenaar (R-MI), who chairs the House Select Committee on China, said he wanted to know whether Huang shared privileged information with Alice Huang and whether he was influenced to lobby against chip export restrictions. "If it becomes less of an investigation, more of damage control, that's not going to work," Moolenaar told CNBC. House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast told ABC News he was prepared to subpoena Huang unless he responded by Wednesday to a request for a closed-door briefing on November 18, the day after Nvidia reports quarterly earnings.
Not everyone in Washington wants the scandal to dominate. Rep. Jay Obernolte (R-CA), co-chair of the House AI task force, told CNBC that a personal scandal should not "interfere" with the policy debate over chip exports to China.
Trump has said the FBI is looking into the matter, and that Huang told him he had no idea the woman was a spy.
Who is Alice Huang?
Alice Huang, who also goes by Huang Le and is not related to Jensen Huang, worked in banking and investment management in China before becoming the controlling shareholder of Singapore-based Megaspeed in March 2023, according to a Reuters review of corporate records and filings.
Megaspeed, which Nvidia lists as a cloud partner, has drawn U.S. scrutiny over whether it helped Chinese firms obtain export-controlled Nvidia chips, but there has been no public finding that it broke the rules, Reuters reported.
China has denied the intelligence allegations, and Reuters said it could not independently verify them. George Chen, a partner at consultancy The Asia Group, told the news agency that Jensen Huang "may also be viewed as a potential victim" if he was targeted without knowing who she was.

articles.title: Bitcoin ETF Outflows Persist as Equity Funds Draw Billions
articles.text:
Stock ETF buyers pounce on dip as Bitcoin funds bleed $1.6 billion
US spot Bitcoin ETFs have lost $1.6 billion in November, while stock funds attracted billions of dollars from investors buying the dip.
US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) recorded $95 million in net outflows on Tuesday as investors poured billions of dollars into stock funds during a market pullback.
Tuesday’s withdrawals brought net outflows from US spot Bitcoin (BTC) ETFs to roughly $1.6 billion since the start of November, according to SoSoValue data.
Bitcoin ETF outflows eased for a third straight session, while stock funds accounted for all 17 of the top US-listed ETFs by inflows over five trading sessions, according to Bloomberg ETF analyst Eric Balchunas.
Equity ETF investors “devoured” the dip
US-listed ETFs attracted roughly $12 billion per day over those five sessions, with all 17 of the top funds by inflows investing in equities, Balchunas said on X on Tuesday.
The biggest beneficiaries included Vanguard’s S&P 500 ETF (VOO), Invesco’s Nasdaq-100 ETF (QQQ) and BlackRock’s iShares Core S&P 500 ETF (IVV).
BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) recorded $78 million in net withdrawals Tuesday, its eighth straight trading session of outflows. The fund recorded about $1.73 billion in net outflows over the streak, according to Farside Investors.
Morgan Stanley’s Bitcoin Trust ETF (MSBT) attracted $20 million Tuesday, although the inflows were insufficient to offset broader losses.
Bitcoin demand weakens as ETF outflows ease
Daily net outflows from Bitcoin ETFs outflows slowed from $430 million Thursday and $412 million Friday to $201 million Monday and $95 million Tuesday, but broader market indicators remained weak, according to CryptoQuant.
CryptoQuant’s Bitcoin Bull Score Index dropped to 20 on Monday from 90 on Oct. 13, signaling “extremely bearish” conditions, according to a Tuesday report seen by Cointelegraph.

The analysts reported that apparent Bitcoin demand contracted by 284,000 BTC over 30 days, the fastest pace since March 2025. articles.title: Bitcoin whales stack coins while ETF investors dump millions daily
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Glassnode found accumulation in two large-wallet groups through Nov. 9, while the other cohorts continued reducing aggregate holdings.
- US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded withdrawals in six of seven completed November sessions, with Nov. 11 flows still unreported.
- The cohort scores measure weighted balance changes, leaving purchase quantities, investor identities and ETF redemption counterparties unresolved.
Bitcoin's latest accumulation signal is concentrated in two large-wallet groups, while US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) continue to record withdrawals.
In its Nov. 11 report, on-chain analytics firm Glassnode identified accumulation in the 100-1,000 BTC and 1,000-10,000 BTC cohorts over the seven-day period through Nov. 9.
These cohorts, grouped by the amount of Bitcoin held, both recorded scores above 0.5. The analytics firm said every other wallet-size cohort was still reducing aggregate holdings, including the largest group above 10,000 BTC and the smallest below 1 BTC.
The newer ETF figures extend that picture through Nov. 10, when the funds recorded net withdrawals of $95 million, according to Farside Investors.
Glassnode said both had spent much of October distributing before returning to accumulation. Their behavior suggests some large holders are adding to their balances, even as participation elsewhere remains weak.
The report added that the same two cohorts turned to accumulation in late September, but the episode did not persist.
Glassnode's seven-day metric weights entity Bitcoin balance size and balance changes over the observation window, excluding exchange and miner entities.
A score near 1 indicates stronger weighted accumulation, while a reading near 0 can indicate distribution or a lack of accumulation.
The Bitcoin balance bands for wallets do not establish beneficial ownership or show whether the holders are institutions, individuals, or buyers using a particular funding source.
ETF withdrawals continue through Nov. 10
Farside's completed November sessions for spot Bitcoin ETFs show withdrawals in six of the seven trading days from Nov. 2 through Nov. 10. Withdrawals resumed after the Nov. 4 inflows and continued in every subsequent completed session shown, including Nov. 9 and 10.
| Completed session | US spot Bitcoin ETF net flow | 
|---|---|
| November 2 | Net outflow of USD 398.6 million | 
| November 3 | Net outflow of USD 115.6 million | 
| November 4 | Net inflow of USD 74.6 million | 
| November 5 | Net outflow of USD 430.2 million | 
| November 6 | Net outflow of USD 411.9 million | 
| November 9 | Net outflow of USD 201 million | 
| November 10 | Net outflow of USD 95 million | 
The cohort score tracks weighted on-chain accumulation, while ETF flows measure net money entering or leaving those funds. Their units cannot be offset to determine whether large-wallet buying covered ETF withdrawals.
Neither dataset connects the accumulating groups to the other side of ETF redemptions, and identifying who acquired Bitcoin associated with those withdrawals would require information these measures don't provide.
A broader improvement would involve more wallet-size groups joining the Bitcoin accumulation signal, alongside sustained net ETF inflows. Those developments would strengthen the case that demand is spreading beyond the two accumulating groups.
For now, the two-cohort turn provides evidence of localized support, with the short-lived late-September accumulation showing why its persistence remains an open test.

articles.title: Avalanche Won Over the NYSE. Now It Has to ‘Capture Value’ for AVAX - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- The NYSE will use Avalanche as the core ledger for clearing and settlement on its planned tokenized securities platform, pending regulatory approval.
- Analysts called it a major credibility win for Avalanche, with one expert noting it came after around a year of testing.
- But the platform will run on dedicated infrastructure rather than the public C-Chain, and experts warn that won’t necessarily translate into value for AVAX.
The New York Stock Exchange this week selected Avalanche to provide infrastructure for a tokenized securities platform it's prepping. Experts say that it's a big deal for Avalanche's reputation, but warn that it may not translate into an uptick in value for the network's AVAX token.
On Monday, Ava Labs announced Avalanche would serve as the "core ledger technology" for a tokenized securities platform developed by NYSE parent company Intercontinental Exchange. The product will be designed to allow 24/7 trading, clearing, and settlement of tokenized securities, subject to regulatory approval.
Carlos Guzman, research analyst at market maker GSR, told Decrypt it’s “definitely a big win for the project.”
“Having NYSE choose its tech for settlement is a big institutional credibility boost, and it validates the benefits blockchain tech can provide to traditional financial plumbing with instant settlement and programmability,” he said.
Luther Maday, head of North America at crypto payments firm Mercuryo, told Decrypt that the decision came after a year of testing on Avalanche, which signals the network passed checks on "performance, reliability, and control."
"NYSE has chosen the technology for the clearing and settlement layer, which is a much deeper use of blockchain than simply issuing a tokenized asset on a network," Maday added.
Avalanche's AVAX token has risen 3.6% in the past day to $8.64, according to Decrypt data. But experts warn that providing infrastructure doesn't necessarily mean a long-term increase in token value.
"NYSE will be using Avalanche’s infrastructure for clearing and settlement, so the actual trading will still happen off-chain," Guzman explained.
This means NYSE activity will run on dedicated Avalanche infrastructure rather than the public C-Chain, where most of the network's activity happens.
"I would be careful about translating the news directly into expectations for activity on the public C-Chain," Maday said.
That said, Maday said to keep an eye on the details of how the AVAX token is used within the dedicated infrastructure. He also suggested that stablecoin liquidity, validator activity, and network fees could see a boost.
The NYSE has also teamed up with Blockchain.com to sell tokenized stocks and ETFs to crypto investors, while its parent company ICE is working with OKX on a 24/7 tokenized stock venue under an SEC exemption. Morgan Stanley, meanwhile, has started tokenizing securities of its own.
Not every company wants in, though. All seven of the so-called "Magnificent Seven" stocks—Apple, Meta, and the like—opted out of having their shares tokenized on the OKX-ICE venue, along with dozens of other companies.
Even if tokenization does take off, that doesn't guarantee profits for AVAX investors.
"The main question for Avalanche is whether it can do what other blockchains have struggled to do: capture value," Misha Putiatin, founder of collateral markets platform Symbiotic, told Decrypt. "Avalanche has always had an unusually outcome-focused team for this industry, so I suspect they have plans for that, but it remains to be seen."
Ava Labs did not immediately respond to Decrypt's request for comment.

articles.title: Bitcoin faces $70,000 test as $14.2 billion stablecoin contraction exposes demand weakness
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Bitcoin faces a fresh liquidity squeeze as stablecoin supply falls $14.2 billion and apparent demand contracts by 284,000 BTC.
- Weak US buying and $1.6 billion in ETF outflows have compounded losses among recent Bitcoin investors, threatening a sustained recovery.
- Bitcoin risks a decline toward $70,000, while a rebound toward $75,600 could prompt underwater holders to sell at breakeven.
Bitcoin is facing a fresh liquidity squeeze as mounting losses among recent buyers threaten to derail its recovery.
Stablecoin supply has contracted by $14.2 billion over the past month, its sharpest decline since June 2022, while Bitcoin's apparent demand has fallen by 284,000 BTC, approaching levels last seen during the March 2025 market turmoil.
The deterioration has left Bitcoin vulnerable to another decline toward $70,000, with investors who purchased at higher prices potentially adding to selling pressure if a recovery fails to attract fresh capital.
Bitcoin's shrinking liquidity pool compounds demand collapse
The retreat in stablecoin supply marks a sharp reversal from the conditions that supported Bitcoin's previous rally.
According to Glassnode's Nov. 11 report, the aggregate supply of dollar-linked tokens declined by $14.2 billion over 30 days, the fastest contraction since the 2022 market crisis.
30-day change in supply of major USD stablecoins, with unresolvable points omitted. Historical readings are approximate monthly and selected event-date samples digitized from the Glassnode chart, rounded to $0.5B.
This corroborates CryptoQuant's earlier research, which showed that Tether's USDT had lost $6.6 billion in market capitalization over 60 days, more than twice the $3.2 billion decline recorded following FTX's collapse in December 2022.
The reversal is particularly striking against the liquidity expansion of the previous two years. USDT's 60-day supply growth peaked at $20.6 billion in December 2024 and generally ranged between $10 billion and $16 billion during much of 2025.
The contraction has coincided with a sharp deterioration in Bitcoin's apparent demand.
CryptoQuant's apparent demand indicator fell to negative 284,000 BTC over 30 days, its weakest reading since March 28, 2025. The measure estimates the difference between newly issued and newly active supply and the amount the market absorbs.
Comparable readings of negative 309,000 BTC in March 2025 and negative 273,000 BTC in June 2026 occurred during earlier market downturns followed by recoveries.
Bitcoin subsequently recovered from its June lows even as the Coinbase Premium Index remained predominantly negative, suggesting the indicator alone was insufficient to capture the rebound's strength.
However, the current downturn has unfolded alongside persistent institutional selling and a broader withdrawal of dollar liquidity.
CryptoQuant found that the Coinbase Premium Index remained negative for 30 consecutive days, averaging approximately minus 0.14%. Glassnode's adjusted measure separately recorded its deepest 30-day discount since February.
US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds have also recorded $1.6 billion in net outflows across 20 trading sessions.
That combination leaves Bitcoin increasingly dependent on buyers willing to absorb supply without the additional support previously provided by expanding stablecoin issuance and ETF inflows.
Bitcoin's recent buyers risk deeper losses toward $70,000
The liquidity contraction is occurring as investors who entered the market during the August and September rally increasingly find themselves holding Bitcoin at a loss.
CryptoQuant data shows that the unrealized profit margin of coins held for one to three months has collapsed from 33% on Sept. 22 to negative 6%. The 39% reversal has left these investors with an average acquisition price near $79,500, against Bitcoin's market price of approximately $74,600 when the research was compiled.
Previous corrections during the current cycle have frequently pushed this profitability measure toward negative 12% before stabilizing. More severe downturns drove it to negative 18% during July to September 2024, negative 19% in April 2025, and negative 23% in July 2026.
At the latest $79,500 acquisition price, a negative 12% margin would put Bitcoin near $70,000, roughly 6% below CryptoQuant's reference price.
Glassnode's broader short-term holder data reveals that only 35% of Bitcoin held by investors who acquired their coins within the past 155 days remains profitable, compared with nearly all such supply at September's high.
Their aggregate cost basis stands near $75,600, while substantial concentrations of Bitcoin purchased between August and October sit at prices extending to $83,600.
A recovery toward those acquisition levels could encourage investors to exit at breakeven, adding to selling pressure in a market already struggling to attract fresh capital.

articles.title: SEC Enforcement Actions Fall 24%, Highlights Crypto Fraud Cases
articles.text:
SEC enforcement actions fall 24%, crypto cases in spotlight
The SEC filed 348 actions in fiscal 2026, down from 456 a year earlier. Cases included alleged Bitcoin mining fraud and an FTX audit settlement.
The US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filed 348 enforcement actions in fiscal 2026, down 23.7% from 456 a year earlier.
Its annual enforcement results included cases involving alleged crypto fraud and failures in FTX’s audits.
In its Tuesday release, the SEC said it had charged three purported crypto trading platforms and four investment clubs in an alleged scheme that defrauded investors of at least $14 million. In a separate case, the agency accused the founder of a Bitcoin mining business of misappropriating $48.5 million after raising more than $95.6 million from about 6,400 investors.
In April, the SEC settled charges against Francis Decker, the Prager Metis partner who led FTX’s audits, over failures to meet professional auditing standards.
In February, a jury found Ismael Zarco Sanchez liable for securities fraud and registration violations over his role in the $300 million CryptoFX Ponzi scheme. In July, a court ordered Michael Noble to pay $1.07 million in a case over his role promoting BitConnect’s crypto lending program.
Fiscal 2026 was SEC Chair Paul Atkins’ first full fiscal year in office. The 348 enforcement actions were the agency’s fewest since 1991, according to a Reuters review of SEC records. Standalone actions fell to 235 from 303 a year earlier.
The decline in crypto enforcement was already visible in 2025, when the SEC filed 13 crypto-related actions, down from 33 in 2024, according to Cornerstone Research. Five of the 13 were filed before former Chair Gary Gensler left office in January 2025.
The SEC said its new enforcement analytics office was using “blockchain and financial-flow analysis” to detect potential misconduct earlier.
Related: SEC flags tokenization as high-risk area in 2027 market examinations

articles.title: Prisoner Jailed for 8 Years Over $2.7M Crypto Theft Plot Run From His Cell - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- A Scottish court has jailed Robert Barr for eight years for orchestrating an attempted theft of up to £2 million ($2.7 million) in crypto from his prison cell.
- Barr planned for two accomplices to make the victim install AnyDesk so he could take control of the computer remotely and move the funds.
- The plot failed when the victims refused to open their door after spotting the men on their doorbell camera.
A man who directed an attempted £2 million ($2.7 million) cryptocurrency theft from his prison cell has been jailed for eight years by Scotland's High Court of Justiciary.
Robert Barr, 29, pleaded guilty along with Sean Favier, 26, and Iain Doyle, 37, to being involved in serious organised crime as part of the attempted theft, according to a sentencing statement published by Scotland's Judicial Office on Tuesday. Lord Cubie sentenced Favier to four years and Doyle to five years at the High Court in Glasgow.
"This was a crime which married 21st century computer sophistication with old fashioned housebreaking in an audacious attempt to steal cryptocurrency worth up to £2 million pounds," Lord Cubie said.
The plan, according to the court's account, was for Favier and Doyle to get into the victims' home in Midlothian, near Edinburgh, and make the man go onto his computer and download AnyDesk, a remote-access program. That would let Barr, who was serving a 21-month sentence at HMP Edinburgh for fraud, take control of the computer from prison and transfer the crypto to wallets he controlled.
The two men went to the house at around 11:30 p.m. on April 17, 2024, but the couple saw them on their doorbell camera and refused to let them in. One of the men looked into the lens and asked whether there was a camera in front of him before the pair left, the BBC reported.
Months of planning
The attempt followed months of preparation, including identifying the victim as a crypto holder, gathering images of the house and reconnaissance, all of which investigators pieced together from Barr's phone after it was seized in June 2024, the judge said. Messages on the phone "plainly contemplated threats and/or violence," he added.
The victim was a co-founder of a crypto startup who did not advertise his holdings, but followed mostly crypto-related accounts on social media, according to the BBC. Barr's associates had already burgled the house in January 2024 and taken a crypto wallet, but could not access the funds without its PIN, the court heard.
Prosecutors described Barr as a "sophisticated cybercriminal" able to "orchestrate a level of criminality rarely seen within mainstream investigations." He had a previous conviction for a crypto fraud, and organised the new offence while in prison "using plainly illicit means of being in contact or online," Lord Cubie said, calling those materially aggravating factors.
The judge said that the plot was only frustrated because the victims "had the sense not to open their front door" to unknown men with their faces covered. Lord Cubie will consider a serious crime prevention order against Barr on November 17. Barr is also in custody awaiting potential extradition, the judge noted.
A rise in wrench attacks
Had the men got inside, the plot would likely have escalated into a so-called wrench attack, in which criminals use force or the threat of it to make crypto holders hand over their funds. Such attacks are on pace for a record year, with more than $30 million stolen in the first half of 2026, according to a Chainalysis report.
The UK has seen several recent cases. Three teenagers were jailed earlier this year after stealing $4.3 million in crypto at knifepoint, and three men were sentenced last month over a failed home invasion aimed at stealing crypto. In September, Crimestoppers offered a reward of up to £10,000 for information on an attack on a UK couple in which, police believe, a fourth man relayed instructions to the three attackers over a video call.
