articles.title: Giá xăng dầu hôm nay 11/11: Thế giới suy yếu, trong nước mai điều chỉnh
articles.text:
Giá dầu thế giới hôm nay
Giá dầu quốc tế trong phiên giao dịch 10/11 được điều chỉnh giảm, xuống mức thấp nhất trong 2 tháng.
Chốt phiên giao dịch 10/11, theo Reuters, giá dầu Brent giảm 1,17%, xuống còn 91,49 USD/thùng. Còn giá dầu WTI hạ 0,9%, kết phiên ở mức 86,04 USD/thùng. Đây là mức đóng cửa thấp nhất của cả hai loại dầu tiêu chuẩn kể từ ngày 31/8.
Đầu phiên giao dịch hôm nay (11/11), giá dầu WTI được điều chỉnh tăng nhẹ.
Theo dữ liệu từ Oilprice, vào lúc 6h28' ngày 11/11 (giờ Việt Nam), giá dầu Brent vẫn được niêm yết ở mức 91,49 USD/thùng. Trong khi đó, giá dầu WTI được điều chỉnh lên mức 86,24 USD/thùng, tăng 0,23% so với phiên liền trước.
Giá dầu thế giới trong phiên 10/11 giảm do những tín hiệu cho thấy căng thẳng giữa Mỹ và Iran có dấu hiệu hạ nhiệt.
Giá dầu đi xuống sau khi các quan chức Mỹ phát tín hiệu chưa cần triển khai thêm các chiến dịch quân sự quy mô lớn nhằm vào Iran, qua đó làm dịu lo ngại về nguy cơ gián đoạn nguồn cung dầu từ Trung Đông.
Bộ trưởng Ngoại giao Mỹ Marco Rubio cho biết đã thông báo với các đồng minh thuộc Nhóm các nước công nghiệp phát triển hàng đầu thế giới (G7) rằng các biện pháp trừng phạt kinh tế và phong tỏa hải quân của Mỹ đang phát huy hiệu quả, qua đó Tổng thống Donald Trump không cần triển khai thêm các hành động quân sự nhằm vào Iran.
Trước đó, ngày 9/11, ông Donald Trump cho biết, ông dự định tạm hoãn các cuộc tấn công quân sự mới nhắm vào Iran, sau khi nhận được lời kêu gọi từ các lãnh đạo trong khu vực, trong đó có Thủ tướng Qatar.
Giới đầu tư cũng đang theo dõi cuộc gặp giữa các quan chức Nga và Ukraine tại Abu Dhabi. Đây là vòng đàm phán hòa bình đầu tiên giữa hai bên kể từ tháng 2, do Mỹ làm trung gian.
Nga hiện là nhà sản xuất dầu thô lớn thứ ba thế giới, sau Mỹ và Arab Saudi. Do đó, nếu hai bên đạt được thỏa thuận hòa bình và Nga gia tăng xuất khẩu dầu thì có thể bổ sung nguồn cung, tạo thêm áp lực giảm giá dầu.
Bên cạnh yếu tố địa chính trị thì những lo ngại về nhu cầu tiêu thụ suy yếu cùng triển vọng nguồn cung được cải thiện tiếp tục tạo sức ép lên giá dầu thế giới.
Số liệu công bố mới đây cho thấy chỉ số giá tiêu dùng tháng 10 tại Mỹ tăng cao hơn dự báo, khiến giới đầu tư lo ngại Cục Dự trữ Liên bang Mỹ (Fed) có thể tiếp tục nâng lãi suất nhằm kiềm chế lạm phát trong cuộc họp vào tháng 12 tới.
Lãi suất cao làm tăng chi phí vay vốn, có thể kìm hãm tăng trưởng kinh tế và thu hẹp nhu cầu tiêu thụ dầu mỏ.
Thêm vào đó, giá năng lượng tăng cao do xung đột tại Trung Đông cũng khiến người tiêu dùng trên toàn thế giới có xu hướng cắt giảm mức sử dụng dầu.
Trong báo cáo mới đây, Cơ quan Thông tin Năng lượng Mỹ (EIA) dự báo nhu cầu tiêu thụ dầu mỏ toàn cầu sẽ giảm từ mức kỷ lục 104,4 triệu thùng/ngày trong năm 2025 xuống còn 102,4 triệu thùng/ngày vào năm 2026.
Giá xăng dầu trong nước hôm nay
Theo kế hoạch, liên bộ Công Thương - Tài chính sẽ tiến hành điều chỉnh giá xăng dầu trong nước vào chiều mai (12/11).
Giá bán của các mặt hàng xăng dầu phổ biến tại thị trường trong nước vào hôm nay (11/11) được áp dụng như sau:
Theo kỳ điều hành ngày 5/11, giá bán lẻ tối đa của xăng E5RON92 giảm 2.305 đồng/lít, từ 23.203 đồng/lít xuống 20.898 đồng/lít.
Tương tự, giá xăng E10RON95-III hạ 2.075 đồng/lít, từ 23.231 đồng/lít xuống còn 21.156 đồng/lít.
Cùng xu hướng, giá dầu diesel 0.05S giảm 180 đồng/lít, từ 28.876 đồng/lít xuống còn 28.696 đồng/lít.
Còn giá dầu mazut 180CST 3.5S hạ 1.969 đồng/kg, từ 23.974 đồng/kg xuống còn 22.005 đồng/kg.
Theo dữ liệu từ Bộ Công Thương, giá bán lẻ xăng dầu tại Việt Nam hiện ở mức thấp hơn so với các nước có chung đường biên giới.
Liên bộ Công Thương - Tài chính đang tiếp tục theo dõi sát diễn biến thị trường để thông báo giá xăng dầu phù hợp với diễn biến thị trường và kịp thời đề xuất Chính phủ, Thủ tướng các giải pháp bình ổn giá xăng dầu.

articles.title: The best early Black Friday deals you can already shop
articles.text:
The countdown to Black Friday is on, and the first discounts are starting to appear. Although the shopping holiday isn’t officially until November 27th, retailers are already dropping early deals on some of our favorite tech. Of course, with prices rising across the board, a good discount doesn’t necessarily mean you’re getting a historically low price. But we’re still seeing worthwhile discounts on a host of tried-and-tested gear, with more expected in the coming weeks.
The best early Black Friday deals you can already shop
Black Friday is still several weeks away, but you can already save on 3D printers, chargers, robot vacuums, and more.
Below, we’ve rounded up the best early Black Friday deals we’ve found so far. Prices could drop further as Black Friday approaches, as is always the case, but these deals are worth considering if you’d rather shop early and beat the holiday rush. We’ll continue to update this guide as more retailers launch their holiday sales, too, so be sure to check back regularly as we get closer to the main event.
Ember Mug 3 (14-ounce)
Ember’s latest smart mug is designed to keep your coffee at the ideal temperature for up to three hours, with five temp settings between 120 and 145 degrees Fahrenheit. The third-gen version is similar to prior models; however, you can now adjust the heat settings directly on the mug and throw it in the dishwasher, which wasn’t the case before.
Hisense CanvasTV (2026)
Hisense’s 2026 CanvasTV is a 4K QLED TV that doubles as wall art when you’re not watching. It features a matte, anti-glare display and runs on Google’s excellent TV software; it’s also a great pick for gamers thanks to its snappy 144Hz variable refresh rate and a pair of HDMI 2.1 ports.
Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 Combo
The Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 Combo is a beginner-friendly 3D printer that supports four filament spools. It features an enclosed build chamber, automatic bed leveling, and a large touchscreen, making it easy to produce reliable prints.
Moft Trackable Tripod Wallet
Moft’s Trackable Tripod Wallet is a MagSafe-compatible wallet that holds two cards and folds into an adjustable phone stand or small tripod. It also supports both Apple’s Find My network and Google’s Find Hub, offers Qi wireless charging, and includes a detachable shutter remote for taking photos.
Govee Christmas String Lights 2
Govee’s Christmas lights offer over 130 preset lighting effects, though you can also create your own custom light displays. The IP65-rated lights feature Matter support, so they’ll work with any major smart home platform, and are sold in lengths up to 328 feet with up to 1,000 LED beads.
Govee Table Lamp 2
Govee’s Table Lamp 2 is way more fun than your average table lamp. The color-changing device boasts built-in scheduling and more than 60 dynamic lighting effects, including preset scenes for various holidays. You can even create custom color combos for when “Dandelion” and other presets just aren’t cutting it.
Birdfy Feeder Metal 2 4K
Birdfy’s metal smart bird feeder features a wide-angle 4K camera that lets you get an up-close look at visiting birds, along with a 1.8-liter seed capacity and a built-in solar panel for charging. It also offers free AI-powered recognition of more than 6,000 bird species.
Tessan Voyager 205 Universal Travel Adapter
Tessan’s universal travel adapter delivers up to 205W of combined USB charging power and can charge up to eight devices, including a pair of laptops, at the same time. It features six USB-C ports, including two that can deliver up to 140W individually, a USB-A port, and an AC outlet. It also works in over 200 countries and regions.
Bambu Lab P2S Combo
Bambu Lab’s P2S Combo is a 3D printer that can print in multiple colors and automatically dry its materials to help improve print quality. It also features a 5-inch touchscreen, a built-in camera for monitoring prints remotely, and AI-powered tools that can detect printing problems.
Dreame X60 Ultra
The Dreame X60 Ultra is a powerful robot vacuum and mop that does a great job of cleaning carpets, thanks to its dual roller brushes and 35,000Pa of suction. It can climb over tall thresholds, squeeze under low furniture, and automatically detach its mop pads when vacuuming carpets.
Eight Sleep Pod 6
Eight Sleep’s Pod 6 automatically adjusts your bed’s temperature based on your sleep patterns, heart rate, and breathing. It features a redesigned hub that’s half the size of its predecessor and adjusts temperatures faster. The system also tracks sleep quality, detects snoring, and lets couples control the temperature on each side of the bed independently.
Flextail Zero Pump 2
Flextail’s Zero Pump 2 might weigh a mere 1.7 ounces, but it can quickly inflate and deflate a sleeping pad. It comes with six nozzles and a replaceable battery that recharges via USB-C, allowing you to inflate up to 30 pads on a single charge.
Litter-Robot 4 Starter Bundle
The last-gen Litter-Robot 4 can monitor your cat’s visits, track their weight, and automatically separate waste from clean litter after each use, so you can go up to eight days without emptying your cat’s litter box. The so-called starter bundle also includes 20 pounds of litter, 25 waste drawer liners, a host of odor-control accessories, a litter-trapping mat, and a three-year warranty.
Headspace subscription
Headspace makes it easier to build mindfulness into your everyday life, whether you’re looking to manage stress, improve focus, or get a better night’s sleep. An annual subscription gives you access to hundreds of guided meditations, breathing exercises, and other tools for beginners and experienced users alike.
Casetify Moonaries illo Edition 2 phone case
Part of Casetify’s early Black Friday sale, which offers up to 50 percent off select phone case styles, this Moonaries Illo case features playful artwork from the illustrator behind Mocha Cat. It’s available for the iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 16 Pro, and other iPhone models.
Sharge Icemag 3 Power Bank
The Icemag 3 can wirelessly deliver up to 25W of power to compatible smartphones and up to 35W wired charging via USB-C. The 10,000mAh Qi2 charger can also act as a foldable kickstand, comes with an integrated USB-C cable that serves as a lanyard, and sports a transparent design with colorful RGB lighting.

articles.title: Google's Tabletop lets groups build AI planning tools together
articles.text:
Google Labs has launched Tabletop, an experiment that builds custom tools such as trip itineraries, dinner polls and expense splitters from a prompt. Groups share one space and edit it together in real time. It is open to US adults via a waitlist.
Google has launched Tabletop, an experiment from its Google Labs team that lets groups build their own planning tools with AI. Google announced the tool on Wednesday.
Users add links, files and ideas to a shared space, then ask @tabletop to build something. It can make trip itineraries, dinner polls, expense splitters and tournament brackets. There are also starter templates.
The creator shares an invite link in a group chat, and everyone can then use the space at the same time. Google compares it to working together in a Google Doc. Group members can vote, plan and track progress in one place.
The tools can also change as plans do. Members can ask @tabletop to change a rule or add something new without starting over. In one example on Google’s product page, a Pong game becomes Pickle Pong, with a bouncing pickle and a live scoreboard.
Google suggests uses such as road trips, sports leagues, weddings, weekly meal plans and school pickups. A chore tracker can even become a game with points and a shared reward.
Tabletop is rolling out in the US to adults aged 18 and over through a waitlist, with new users let in each week. Google has not said which AI model powers it.
Google Labs experiments sometimes become full products. NotebookLM started there and was renamed Gemini Notebook this year. Google has also opened its Play Store to AI-built apps, while Slack now lets teams build with AI agents inside its chat app.

articles.title: AWS open-sources UAEF, a tool to test AI agents across frameworks
articles.text:
AWS has released UAEF, a free open-source tool that tests AI agents on 36 measures, from tool use to safety. It works across several agent frameworks and flags when a new prompt or model makes an agent worse.
Amazon Web Services has released a free tool that tests whether changes to an AI agent made it better or worse. The Universal Agent Evaluation Framework (UAEF) is open source, AWS said in a blog post on Wednesday.
AI agents are built with different software kits, such as LangGraph, LangChain, Strands Agents and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Each one records an agent’s steps in its own format. That means teams often have to rebuild their testing whenever they switch tools.
UAEF converts those records into one shared format, then scores the agent on 36 measures in seven areas. These include how well it picks and uses tools, the quality of its answers, safety, speed, and how it handles long conversations or teamwork with other agents. Some scores are calculated directly, while others are judged by a second AI model on Amazon Bedrock.
Teams can save each test run and compare it with an earlier one. Any score that drops by more than 5% is flagged as a regression and rated minor, moderate or severe. AWS says 12 organisations in telecoms, healthcare and financial services have used UAEF to compare agent versions before release.
The tool is free to use, but scoring with AI judges and saving results both rely on AWS services. AWS also warns that UAEF should not be used to make security decisions.
Getting agents to work reliably remains a struggle. AWS has said almost 90% of prototypes Amazon built two years ago never shipped. Startups such as Raindrop have raised money to catch agent failures in production.
Researchers have also shown that one prompt could take over AgentCore agents, which AWS disputed.

articles.title: Diện mạo bãi biển đẹp nhất châu Á sau khi Đà Nẵng chi gần 1.200 tỷ 'hồi sinh'
articles.text:
XEM CLIP: Biển Cửa Đại hồi sinh ngoạn mục sau hơn 10 năm bị sóng xâm thực
Biển Cửa Đại (phường Hội An Đông, TP Đà Nẵng) từng được TripAdvisor bình chọn vào nhóm 25 bãi biển được yêu thích ở châu Á. Tuy nhiên, từ khoảng năm 2014, tình trạng xói lở diễn biến nghiêm trọng tại nhiều đoạn bờ biển. Sóng biển cuốn trôi cát, làm thu hẹp bãi tắm, gây hư hại một số công trình ven bờ và ảnh hưởng đến hoạt động du lịch, kinh doanh dịch vụ của người dân.
Tháng 3/2025, tỉnh Quảng Nam khởi công dự án Chống xói lở và bảo vệ bền vững bờ biển Hội An, với tổng mức đầu tư hơn 982 tỷ đồng. Đến tháng 4/2026, TP Đà Nẵng tiếp tục triển khai công trình khắc phục khẩn cấp tuyến kè bảo vệ sông Thu Bồn khu vực An Lương và khắc phục xói lở bờ biển Hội An, giá trị hơn 214 tỷ đồng.
Tổng mức đầu tư của dự án chống xói lở bờ biển Hội An và giá trị gói thầu xử lý xói lở thuộc công trình khắc phục khẩn cấp nói trên đạt khoảng 1.196 tỷ đồng.
Các công trình bảo vệ bờ cùng hoạt động tôn tạo bãi tắm đã góp phần khôi phục cảnh quan Cửa Đại, tạo điều kiện để du lịch và dịch vụ ven biển phục hồi.
Từ trên cao, bãi biển Cửa Đại hiện lên với dải cát trải dài, hàng dừa xanh và các khu nghỉ dưỡng ven biển. Ngoài khơi là hệ thống đê ngầm giảm sóng được xây dựng nhằm hạn chế tác động của sóng biển, góp phần bảo vệ và ổn định đường bờ.
Cách bờ biển gần 300m, hệ thống 7 tuyến đê ngầm giảm sóng có tổng chiều dài hơn 2km được bố trí song song với bờ. Công trình được thiết kế nhằm giảm năng lượng sóng, hạn chế tình trạng cát bị cuốn trôi và hỗ trợ ổn định bãi biển.
Năm 2015, nhiều đoạn bờ biển Cửa Đại bị sóng đánh sạt lở, hàng quán ven biển phải dùng bao cát, bạt và cọc tre để bảo vệ.
Sau khi các hạng mục chống xói lở được triển khai, nhiều đoạn bờ biển được gia cố bằng hệ thống kè, không gian ven bờ cũng được chỉnh trang, tạo diện mạo khang trang hơn.
Dọc bờ biển, tuyến kè bê tông nhiều bậc chạy dài bên hàng dừa xanh. Phía trên là lối đi rộng rãi, kết nối các cơ sở dịch vụ và khu nghỉ dưỡng.
Các cấu kiện bê tông được xếp thành nhiều lớp, tạo thành tuyến kè bảo vệ bờ biển. Công nhân đang hoàn thiện những hạng mục còn lại để phục vụ công tác nghiệm thu, bàn giao công trình.
Dưới những hàng dừa xanh, tuyến đường ven biển trở thành nơi người dân và du khách đi dạo, hóng mát, tập thể dục vào sáng sớm và chiều muộn.
Dọc lối đi ven biển, nhiều du khách nước ngoài thư giãn trên những chiếc ghế dài dưới bóng dừa.
Chị Adeline, du khách đến từ Pháp, cho biết ấn tượng với bãi cát rộng, hàng dừa xanh và không gian yên bình ở Cửa Đại. Sau khi biết về tình trạng xói lở từng diễn ra tại đây, chị khá bất ngờ. “Tôi thích đi dạo, ngắm sóng và tận hưởng không khí trong lành ở nơi này”, chị chia sẻ.
Bãi cát rộng trải dài ven biển Cửa Đại sau quá trình triển khai các công trình chống xói lở và tôn tạo bãi tắm, tạo thêm không gian cho du khách vui chơi, nghỉ dưỡng.
Ghế nghỉ, dù lá và các thiết bị phục vụ thể thao biển được bố trí dọc bãi cát, tạo thêm lựa chọn vui chơi, thư giãn cho du khách.
Nhiều người dân và du khách vẫn đến Cửa Đại tắm biển, vui chơi, ngay cả trong thời điểm du lịch không cao điểm.
Ông Lê Hoàng Chương, thành viên đội cứu hộ bãi biển Cửa Đại, cho biết lượng người đến tắm biển có dấu hiệu tăng lên sau khi các công trình chống xói lở được triển khai. Hoạt động kinh doanh dịch vụ ven bờ cũng dần sôi động hơn.
Một người bán hàng giới thiệu đồ lưu niệm cho du khách trên bậc kè ven biển. Những hoạt động mua bán nhỏ góp phần tạo nên nhịp sống thường ngày tại khu vực này.
Những chiếc thuyền thúng nằm trên bãi cát, phía xa là du khách dạo biển. Hình ảnh quen thuộc của vùng biển Hội An tạo thêm nét đặc trưng cho điểm đến này.
Những bãi cát rộng dần trở lại, các hoạt động tắm biển và dịch vụ ven bờ từng bước được khôi phục, mang đến kỳ vọng mới cho du lịch Cửa Đại và sinh kế của người dân địa phương.

articles.title: Ocarina of Time is even better if you use a smartphone app
articles.text:
I never liked hunting for Golden Skulltulas in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. The game has 100 of them tucked all over Hyrule, and even over my many hours with the N64 classic growing up, I can’t remember ever actually finding all of them, or even wanting to. Jumping into the Ocarina of Time remake, I expected to ignore the Golden Skulltulas once again. But while poking around Nintendo’s Zelda Notes companion app, I discovered that its maps are a huge help to tracking down all of the elusive golden spiders — and pretty much every other collectible in the game — and now I find myself constantly opening up the app to make sure I haven’t missed a secret.
Ocarina of Time is even better if you use a smartphone app
Finding Ocarina of Time’s hidden collectibles is a lot easier with the help of Zelda Notes.
Inside Zelda Notes, which is available in the free Nintendo Switch app (you don’t need a Switch Online subscription to use it), you can peruse a big map of Hyrule and tap on individual areas for a closer look. The app offers just enough direction to nudge me toward an elusive pickup; when zoomed in, the app drops icons on the map showing you the locations of different collectibles, and if you tap on an icon, the app will show a popup noting any items or special requirements you need to fulfill to be able to obtain it. There are also a bunch of filters you can apply, like swapping between the maps for child and adult Link and toggling categories of icons on and off.
For Skulltula hunting, the map has already saved my sanity many times. While exploring, I’ll often come across the telltale Golden Skulltula sound but have no idea how to get to the tricky spider, even with the help of additional chimes from the new Echo Gem Skulltula tracking item. But with a peek at the Zelda Notes app, I can pinpoint the exact location of where the Skulltula is supposed to be and if I need to use a certain item or change the time of day to be able to get to it.
I recently delved into the Shadow Temple, for example, and I couldn’t figure out how to get up to a Skulltula that I saw while coming down an elevator. But when I checked the icon on the Zelda Notes map, it said that I needed the Scarecrow Song to create a hookshot point, which I hadn’t gotten yet. As soon as I finished the dungeon, getting the Scarecrow Song was my first priority.
Zelda Notes has been useful for tracking down Pieces of Heart, too, which give Link more health once you collect enough. While running up and down Zora’s River, I kept seeing two Pieces of Heart on faraway ledges that I couldn’t figure out how to get to. (My memories of my extensive time with Ocarina of Time as a kid also failed me.) But tapping one of the icons on the Zelda Notes map revealed that I needed a Cucco to get to it — and suddenly, I understood why there was one of the chirping white birds near the entrance of the zone.
Yes, it can be annoying to have to open my phone and dig through an app to track down all of the Skulltulas and other objects of curiosity scattered around Hyrule. I play video games to try and get away from my phone, not look at it more. And sure, I could just look up an online guide, but that often means wading through walkthroughs of varying quality, trusting an AI summary, or scrubbing through a YouTube video. But with Zelda Notes, I’m usually in and out relatively quickly, putting down my phone after seeing a clue or an icon that pushes me in the direction of the next golden spider. I’ve already found more than 70 Golden Skulltulas, and to my surprise, I now want to hunt for the full 100.

articles.title: StitchStudio raises $8M for AI agents that do insurers' paperwork
articles.text:
StitchStudio has raised $8M led by Voyager Capital to expand its AI agents for insurance carriers and brokers. The agents handle tasks such as quote comparison and billing checks inside existing systems, and every action can be audited.
StitchStudio, an Oregon startup that builds AI agents for insurers, has raised $8M in a round led by Voyager Capital, the company announced on Wednesday. Lookout Ventures and Grit Capital Partners joined, along with earlier backers ManchesterStory and BrokerTech Fund. The company raised a $3M seed round in 2025.
The money will go into new products for employee benefits, life insurance and annuities, and commercial property cover. StitchStudio will also hire more customer support staff and build self-service tools.
Insurers often run old and new systems side by side, so staff end up typing the same data into several screens. StitchStudio’s agents connect to those systems rather than replacing them, and each action they take can be traced and audited.
Customers include M3 Insurance, Heffernan Insurance Brokers and Fidelity Life. They use the agents for tasks such as comparing quotes, onboarding sales agents and checking bills.
“Our customers got their first workflows live and came back to expand across the enterprise. This round helps us get them there faster,” said CEO Karan Mishra.
StitchStudio says one customer cut proposal turnaround from 90 minutes to 15. At Heffernan, staff still choose insurers and advise clients, while the software gathers and compares the data.
Investors are backing a growing number of insurance AI startups. London’s Ancep raised $8.5M for broker agents this week, while Corridor launched with $25M for benefits. Big insurers are buying in too, with Guardian handing 1 million dental calls a year to AI agents.

articles.title: Google’s AlphaGenome 2 zooms in on the cellular roots of disease
articles.text:
Researchers at Google DeepMind have unveiled a new AI model designed to unravel how changes in our DNA affect different cells, giving scientists a more detailed view of a notoriously difficult problem that could hold important clues to the causes of disease — and point the way to new treatments.
Google’s AlphaGenome 2 zooms in on the cellular roots of disease
DeepMind’s new DNA model better predicts how mutations affect different cells, potentially opening paths to treatment.
AlphaGenome 2 is the successor to DeepMind’s genome-predicting AI model AlphaGenome, which was released last year. While nearly every cell in the human body carries the same DNA, different types of cells — from heart muscle cells and skin cells to immune cells fighting an infection — switch different genes on and off, and those patterns can change depending on what a cell is doing. As a result, the same genetic variant can have very different effects depending on the type and state of the cell.
The new model is designed to capture those differences, predicting the effects of genetic variants on individual cell types and states. Google said in a blog post published Wednesday that it offers a much finer-grained view than broader models like AlphaGenome, potentially revealing disease-relevant effects in specific cells that might otherwise go unnoticed.
AlphaGenome 2 was trained on more than 100 million individual cell profiles across 68 tissues to give it that more detailed view. DeepMind says the model effectively turns static cell atlases — huge data repositories that map and catalog individual cells in detail — “into a predictive engine for human genetics.” According to the company, AlphaGenome 2 identifies nearly twice as many variants that can change gene expression in cells than its previous state-of-the-art model.
Notably, the researchers found that AlphaGenome 2 could also make predictions about new types of cells and biological states without needing to be retrained. It could also identify gaps in experimental data, potentially helping scientists decide what to investigate next in the lab.
For Adam Gayoso, a research scientist at Google DeepMind involved in the project, the big breakthrough is “tying human genetics to cell biology.” AlphaGenome 2 gives researchers a way to drill down on genetic variants identified in large populations, to see what effects they may be having on a cellular level, and potentially connect those effects to disease, he told The Verge.
Google DeepMind’s genomics lead Žiga Avsec told The Verge that this specificity is important if you have a goal like figuring out how to treat a particular disease. “When you develop drugs, you’re targeting specific proteins and specific cell types,” he explained, which makes having this kind of granularity vital.
Building a model like AlphaGenome 2 has only recently become possible thanks to new technologies that can capture individual cells and their states at high resolution and create the vast datasets needed to train it, Avsec said. DeepMind is now working to improve its genetics models by generating more data, including for cell states that aren’t represented well today. Avsec said future versions could also potentially be trained on data “across multiple species,” giving the models a broader view of biology. Longer term, he said models like AlphaGenome 2 could feed into efforts to create “virtual cells,” digital simulations designed to mimic biological systems.
Although Avsec said he views AlphaGenome 2 as a successor to AlphaGenome, it isn’t replacing it any time soon. He said its more detailed predictions come at a computational cost and are “more expensive” to produce than those of its predecessor, he said. Those demands would have made it impractical to use AlphaGenome 2 to produce the genome-wide Atlas covering “every possible DNA letter change in the human genome” that DeepMind released in September.
Google says it is making AlphaGenome 2 available for non-commercial research via the AlphaGenome API from today, with a limited “private preview” for commercial research.
The model is the latest in a growing array of efforts by Google and rival AI labs to use the technology to tackle major problems in science and medicine. Pushmeet Kohli, who heads DeepMind’s AI for science research, has hinted that more impressive scientific results are on the way, and the organization is expected to open an automated materials science lab in the UK soon. Anthropic, meanwhile, has been experimenting with drug design and given Claude a wet lab, while OpenAI has been mowing down an impressive amount of longstanding problems in mathematics and related fields.

articles.title: CCTV Script 12/11/26
articles.text:
– This is the script of CNBC's financial news report for China's CCTV on November 12, 2026.
Behind the European Union's push for these new regulations lies a widening gap between existing consumer protection rules and emerging issues in the digital consumer market. EU Justice Commissioner McGrath, who leads the bill, noted that most EU consumer protection laws were drafted prior to the rise of e commerce, influencer marketing, and the attention economy. Today, unfair practices such as hidden fees and difficult subscription cancellations cost consumers roughly 10.3 billion euros annually at a time when many households are already grappling with living cost pressures.
While the consumer protection focus is welcomed, some organizations argue that the draft legislation remains insufficiently strict. The proposal does not impose a comprehensive ban on addictive features like auto play, nor does it explicitly restrict designs aimed at prolonging user engagement via artificial intelligence. Instead, it merely mandates that platforms offer an opt out toggle, which could introduce significant future uncertainty and trigger drawn out, case by case reviews.
However, for platforms such as Meta, once users actively opt out of these features, user dwell time on platforms could shrink, squeezing advertising revenue potential.
PAUL MUSGRAVE
Associate Professor of Government
Georgetown University in Qatar
"The EU has historically taken a very consumer focused privacy protection realm. I'm not saying that that's good or bad. But it is something that hinders these sorts of things."
Additionally, the draft has sparked industry concerns regarding regulatory complexity and user privacy. The Computer and Communications Industry Association pointed out that while a unified EU wide regulation could help reduce legal discrepancies among member states, introducing new rules before existing frameworks such as the Digital Services Act and the General Data Protection Regulation are consistently enforced will generate legislative duplication and enforcement confusion. Furthermore, because the draft expands the definition of vulnerable consumers by requiring platforms to detect whether users are in states of addiction or financial distress, practical execution could force platforms to escalate user behavior tracking and process more sensitive personal data.
Nevertheless, the draft legislation must be reviewed and approved by EU member states and the European Parliament before officially becoming law. The European Commission estimates that if successfully implemented, the new measures could save consumers up to 13.7 billion euros in unnecessary expenses annually.

articles.title: Cramer's stance on Nvidia's stock amid reports that CEO Jensen Huang may be ousted
articles.text: Jim Cramer said Wednesday night that he was saddened by a news report that indicated Nvidia's board of directors is preparing to fire CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang amid a widening extramarital affair scandal. "Look, a Jensen-less Nvidia is an Nvidia many will not want to own," Jim said on "Mad Money," as not one but two bombshell articles were hitting the tape and the stock started sinking in after-hours trading. "I've always said, 'own it, don't trade it.' Well, I didn't think [anything like] this would happen. I don't know anyone who did. It's very sobering." After the show, Jim indicated that at this point he doesn't want to buy any more shares of Nvidia into the scandal-driven sell-off, nor does he want to sell ahead of next Tuesday's earnings report. However, he did express a belief that the company can still succeed over the long term even if it is without Huang at the helm. Shares of Nvidia fell more than 8% in extended trading Wednesday after The Wall Street Journal reported that the chipmaker's board was preparing to oust Huang, with plans to meet as soon as Wednesday to discuss his future. The Journal's story landed shortly after The New York Times reported that Huang had an affair with an executive who reports to him, Kimberly Powell, the chip giant's vice president of healthcare. Nvidia did not immediately respond to the Club's request for comment on Wednesday's reporting from The Journal and The Times. The reports came on top of The Times reporting Sunday that Nvidia's board was investigating an affair that Huang admitted to having with an executive at Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed — a woman U.S. intelligence agencies believe is a Chinese spy. On Tuesday, Nvidia's board said it hired the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to lead the inquiry. The Club has owned a position in Nvidia since 2019, years before the company's graphics processing units helped enable the generative AI boom, turning Nvidia into a juggernaut stock and vaulting Huang into rockstar CEO status. We downgraded our rating on Nvidia to a hold-equivalent 2 on Tuesday due to the uncertainty around Huang's future at the company. Earlier Wednesday, we said we wanted to initiate a position in rival Advanced Micro Devices due, in part, to a belief that AMD will win business as a result of the Huang scandal. However, our restrictions — which prevent us from trading any stock that Jim mentions on CNBC for a 72-hour period — stood in our way. We did, however, add AMD to our Bullpen watchlist , reflecting our intentions to initiate a stake once our restrictions lift. We also plan to exit Intel , while building up an AMD position. Jim said he vastly prefers AMD over Nvidia in this moment. Nevertheless, Jim said his experience watching Apple thrive after the death of co-founder and visionary CEO Steve Jobs is one reason why he doesn't want to blow out of Nvidia despite Huang potentially no longer serving as its chief executive. Tim Cook took Apple to even greater heights during his 15-year tenure, before passing the torch to now-CEO John Ternus on Sept. 1. Despite Huang's close association with Nvidia, Jim said he believes there is plenty of talent inside the company that can step into a potential leadership vacuum. In particular, he mentioned Ian Buck, a vice president who created the CUDA software program that was integral in Nvidia evolving from a video-game chip company into a data center and AI titan. articles.title: How much Jensen Huang is worth to Nvidia’s stock
articles.text: Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang's future as head of one of the most important names in technology hangs in the balance following revelations that he had an affair with a woman who U.S. intelligence agencies say is a Chinese spy. On Wednesday afternoon, The New York Times reported that Huang is also said to have had a relationship with an executive at Nvidia who reported to him, casting a further shadow over his leadership of the company. Minutes after that news broke, The Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia's board is preparing to remove Huang . Huang issued an apology on Sunday after The New York Times reported that he had an extramarital relationship with a woman intelligence agencies identified as a spy . Nvidia shares fell nearly 10% over the first two trading days of the week before rebounding in Wednesday's regular session. Shares were last down 8% in extended trading following the Journal's report that the CEO's future at Nvidia may be in jeopardy. NVDA 5D mountain Nvidia in the past five trading days If Huang has to leave the company, Nvidia stock could take a major hit, Wall Street analysts and investors told CNBC. "When you have a founder-led company, and there's no clear number two, that is a recipe for a 20% correction," Gene Munster, managing partner at Deepwater Asset Management, said. Jay Goldberg at Seaport Research Partners also said that the stock could see a 20% hit following a sudden departure of Huang, but he suggested it could fall a lot more due to the CEO's managerial centrality at the company. "If he gets fired tomorrow, or whatever happens to him tomorrow, the stock is down 20%," he said. "But that's just the near-term impact – the shock value. He's built this company. He founded it. He's grown it to where it is. He's the only CEO the company's ever had, and he structured the company in such a way [that] he is at the center of everything. He has 70 direct reports." Dented valuation Matt Bryson at Wedbush made a comparison on Nvidia's valuation to that of wafer maker TSMC, which supplies many of Nvidia's core components. "If you look at Taiwan Semi ... At the beginning of the day, it was trading at 15 times next year's numbers [earnings], and I think Nvidia was closer to 10. So, I mean, you could make an argument there that that delta is largely, or at least in part attributable to concerns around his [Huang's] future," he said. Huang's scandal wouldn't be the first time that a company's stock took a hit as a result of reported marital affairs or espionage claims involving a CEO. Many different companies have taken a hit on similar news, according to research from Mizuho. Despite the risks to the stock, analysts said that Nvidia is still solidly positioned to continue its operations in the event that Huang has to step down. "Can it be managed forward? That's the real question. I think it can, because Jensen has instilled, has set the company up to succeed. He set the pace, set the tone, and established such deep, entrenched relationships and agreements within the industry that if he left, I don't think anything would change at Nvidia for at least the next couple years," said Cody Acree, an analyst at StoneX. Gil Luria of D.A. Davidson said there may not be any substantive long-term effect on the company provided there's a solid transition plan in place for Huang. "If he has to leave … if there's good succession and an orderly transition, I don't think there's going to be any impact to the company," he said. – Paulina Likos contributed reporting

articles.title: Inside India newsletter: Trump's poll setback fuels hope for U.S.-India trade deal by year end
articles.text:
Hello, this is Priyanka Salve, writing to you from India.
Welcome to the latest edition of "Inside India" — your one-stop destination for stories and developments from the world's fastest-growing large economy.
After months of being weighed down by high energy prices, trade uncertainty and foreign investor exodus, India has had plenty to celebrate this Diwali. Foreign investors returned to its market in November and, now, it seems the long-awaited U.S.-India trade deal could be around the corner.
Experts say that the two sides are closer to signing on the dotted line following the U.S. midterm election results than they were before.
Any thoughts on today's newsletter? Share them with the team.
The big story
The U.S.-India trade deal, which has been riddled with uncertainty since February, is likely to get a final push to the finish line, thanks to U.S. President Donald Trump's electoral setback in the midterm polls.
Experts told CNBC that Trump could lean toward closing some of the pending trade deals to promote them as policy achievements to the American public, and the pact with New Delhi is a "prime candidate."
They added that Trump and Indian Prime Minister Modi are likely to sign the trade pact when they meet in December for the G20 leaders meeting, as negotiations have largely concluded.
The U.S.-India trade talks "are far along and there seems to be a gentlemen's agreement between Trump and Modi" that the deal should be concluded when the two meet at Mar-a-Lago in December, Mark Linscott, former assistant U.S. trade representative and senior advisor at the U.S.-India Strategic Partnership Forum, told CNBC.
Trump has used tariffs as a pressure tactic to clinch trade deals with several countries, even as that approach has drawn the ire of his political opponents who have flagged that export levies have increased costs for American households. Cost of living was the top concern for American voters in the midterms.
"The election was a verdict on the cost of living, and tariffs are now a liability the President cannot defend on the numbers," Ronak D. Desai, visiting fellow at Hoover Institution of Stanford University, told CNBC.
"Congress will not hand him an affordability win, but a trade deal is one he can announce on his own," Desai said, adding that an announcement of a deal with India is "more likely than it was before the election."
India's commerce and external affairs ministries and the U.S. Trade Representative's Office did not respond to CNBC's requests for comment.
When asked about how U.S. midterm election results will reshape the ties with New Delhi, a spokesperson for India's Ministry of External Affairs on Tuesday said that the relationship between the two countries "enjoys bipartisan support in the United States."
Hard bargain
Trump insists Americans do not share the burden of his tariffs, but according to estimates from Tax Foundation, a nonprofit, the duties raised the average U.S. household's tax burden by $820 in 2026 and $1,000 in 2025.
As a result, the Democrats, within days of taking control of both the houses of Congress are preparing to challenge Trump's signature tariff policy. A trade deal at this time could be seen as a validation of Trump's tariffs-led approach to business.
"The president may lean more into getting deals done – seeing them as policy achievements that he can promote to the American public," Atman Trivedi, partner at Washington-based DGA Albright Stonebridge Group, told CNBC. He added that the Trump administration would like to get a deal done with India by the G20 leaders' summit in December.
While American voters are more affected by import duties on Canadian goods, experts said that a trade deal with India could blunt criticism about tariffs as an effective bargaining chip.
In February, Trump announced a deal with India, claiming that New Delhi had agreed to "Buy American" at a much higher level after the U.S. agreed to slash tariffs to 18%. Trump had earlier imposed a 25% tariff on imports from India, along with an additional 25% duty on goods from New Delhi for buying Russian oil.
But that deal has since been awaiting final approval, especially after the Supreme Court struck down Trump tariffs, giving India space to demand preferential tariffs that give it an edge over competitors.
While American and Indian officials at the start of October said that the negotiations had reached an impasse, Trump on Oct. 20 said that the two sides were "pretty close" to a final deal. As per Indian media reports, the country's Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal confirmed that discussions on the trade deal had largely "concluded."
"We have been hearing for weeks that a deal is close to be settled," Aryan D'Rozario, associate fellow and chair on India and Emerging Asia Economics at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, told CNBC, adding that Modi's visit to the G20 summit in December "will provide the perfect stage to formalize an agreement."
Need to know.
India as an AI hedge? The country's stocks could see robust inflows as markets globally tank
The Indian stock market is emerging as an attractive hedge as investors seek refuge from a brutal sell-off in the artificial intelligence trade, making it a strong contender for global capital. If global investors "neutralize" their underweight positions on India, it could lead to foreign inflows of $115 billion, as per JPMorgan.
India billionaire Adani's firm buys Dutch firm Evos to gain foothold in Europe
Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone, India's largest port operator, will acquire Netherlands-headquartered Evos from Igneo Infrastructure Partners in an all-cash deal at an enterprise value of 2.56 billion euros.

Nov.15: India unemployment rate for October.

articles.title: Jim Cramer says investors need to pay attention to CoreWeave. Here's why
articles.text:
CNBC's Jim Cramer said Wednesday that he's becoming less skeptical of CoreWeave after the neocloud's strong earnings and the CEO's "refreshing and reassuring" comments.
CoreWeave shares surged nearly 25% on Wednesday after the company reported better-than-expected quarterly revenue and raised its 2026 guidance. The results, which were out Tuesday evening, helped ease concerns about a slowdown in AI infrastructure spending. CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator's subsequent interview with Cramer on CNBC just after Wall Street's opening bell offered further reasons for optimism.
One of the most encouraging takeaways from Intrator was disclosure that demand for CoreWeave's computing capacity is 10 times greater than what the company can supply. It was also discussed on the post-earnings conference call. That dynamic has allowed CoreWeave to consistently increase prices, supporting stronger gross margins even as it spends heavily to expand its infrastructure.
Intrator also addressed concerns about CoreWeave's substantial debt load, which has weighed heavily on its stock. Despite Wednesday's surge, shares are still down 15% year to date and down 55% from its 52-week high of $138 on May 6. The past month has been particularly tumultuous for the neoclouds, which also include Iren and Nebius. Iren reported strong earnings last week. Nebius reports its quarter Thursday morning.
Rather than relying solely on traditional bond markets, CoreWeave has increasingly turned to financing backed by its equipment and customer contracts. "When I pressed him, asking why he doesn't just go into the open market and buy these bonds that are trading so poorly, he admitted that he's been tempted to, but ultimately he still believes he can make an even better return building data centers," Cramer said. "Take that red flag off the table."
Another surprising revelation involved the value of CoreWeave's Nvidia chips. Intrator said some H100 chips purchased four years ago are now being contracted at premiums of 20% to 50% above its original cost, suggesting the equipment is retaining its economic value longer than many investors anticipated.
The Intrator interview also helped ease concerns about growing political opposition to data center construction. The CEO maintained that demand for computing power would continue to drive expansion, even if stricter regulations pushed some projects overseas.
For Cramer, the comments offered a welcome counterpoint to the recent pessimism surrounding AI infrastructure stocks. While he has grown more cautious about the sector amid political and financing risks, the "Mad Money" host maintained that abandoning it altogether could mean missing substantial upside. "We've taken some data center and related stocks off the table, unfortunately not Nvidia, [for the CNBC Investing Club] because our composure and our prudence dictates that to have too much data center is still too dicey. Still, we've left plenty of exposure to the group, which includes semis, software, networking, builders, turbines and cooling equipment, because we think the AI theme has much more room to run."
The Club does not own any neoclouds. But it does have diversified, albeit recently reduced, exposure to the AI boom via chip stocks and names that help run and power data centers.

articles.title: Jim Cramer: This is the bet you're making if you buy the Anthropic IPO
articles.text:
Anthropic has reached a major profitability milestone ahead of its expected blockbuster initial public offering next week. But CNBC's Jim Cramer warned Wednesday that the frontier AI lab's future spending commitments could make staying profitable a much bigger challenge.
"Anthropic is due to spend an enormous amount in the future, so it needs to continue growing rapidly to outrun those costs and remain profitable," the "Mad Money" host said. "That's the bet you're making if you buy the Anthropic IPO."
The Claude developer became profitable on an adjusted operating basis for the first time in the second quarter of 2026 and remained positive in the third. Through the first nine months of 2026, Anthropic's adjusted operating income totaled $4.08 billion, according to its IPO prospectus. In calculating its adjusted operating income, Anthropic excludes stock-based compensation, noncash charitable contributions, and payments tied to a class-action copyright lawsuit settlement, according to its IPO prospectus. When following generally accepted accounting principles, or GAAP, Anthropic had an operating loss of $1.26 billion through the third quarter of this year.
"To be clear, Anthropic achieving profitability, even on this adjusted operating income basis, is no small matter," Cramer said.
Another big difference between Anthropic's adjusted results and GAAP numbers appears when looking at net income. This metric appears at the bottom of a company's income statement and serves as the basis for calculating its earnings per share. For 2026, Anthropic reported a net loss of more than $104 billion through September, compared with adjusted net income of $5.6 billion.
Much of that difference reflects a $94 billion noncash charge tied to the rising value of securities issued to partners such as Google and Amazon. Those arrangements have allowed Anthropic to secure computing resources without immediately paying cash, helping preserve much of the capital it has raised. Cramer cautioned against dismissing those charges entirely, arguing they reflect infrastructure costs the company would otherwise have paid in cash.
Indeed, Cramer emphasized that investors cannot ignore Anthropic's purchase commitments and lease agreements for computing infrastructure. As of September, Anthropic has committed to spending in the future approximately $900 billion, largely on computing infrastructure, according to its prospectus.
Anthropic's spending commitments include an agreement with SpaceX worth up to $120.5 billion through 2029, alongside deals with Alphabet's Google, Amazon, Microsoft and other computing providers. Roughly half of its $900 billion in commitments is expected to come due by the end of 2030. About $70 billion is expected over the next year alone.
"Long story short, Anthropic's compute costs — its cash compute costs — are going to explode," Cramer said.
In its IPO roadshow presentation, Anthropic projected that computing and infrastructure expenses would eventually account for 45% to 50% of revenue, supporting a long-term adjusted operating margin of roughly 35%.
Cramer's key point Wednesday is that reaching that margin target will require sustained revenue growth. On Tuesday, Cramer highlighted Anthropic's 1,206% year over year revenue growth during the first nine months of 2026, but the company will need to keep growing rapidly to stay ahead of its mounting infrastructure costs.
"You have to assume that this company's going to continue growing substantially – to the point where it has hundreds of billions of revenue per year, and soon," Cramer said Wednesday. "That's the only way this works."
The stakes extend beyond Anthropic itself. On Monday, Cramer warned that the company's IPO could be a crucial test for the broader AI trade, given how heavily companies depend on its continued spending.
Anthropic is expected to price its IPO on Nov. 18 and begin trading on the Nasdaq on Nov. 19, CNBC's Leslie Picker reported Tuesday.

articles.title: Scott Colom wins Mississippi Senate election over incumbent Republican Hyde-Smith
articles.text:
Democratic nominee Scott Colom won the Mississippi Senate election over Republican incumbent Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, the Associated Press reported Wednesday.
Colom, a local district attorney, will be the first Black senator from Mississippi since the post-Civil War Reconstruction Era.
His projected victory — which was not considered likely by national analysts before Election Day — is the latest in a series of stunning wins by Democrats this midterm cycle.
Two sources close to Colom's campaign said Hyde-Smith called him late Wednesday afternoon to concede.
"While this is not the outcome we worked for, or hoped for, I respect the decision of Mississippi voters," Hyde-Smith said in a video posted on X.
"I want to congratulate Scott Colom and wish him well as he takes on the tremendous responsibility of representing our great state," Hyde-Smith said.
Democrats now will have a majority of at least 55 seats in the Senate, having flipped at least eight seats from Republicans.
Alaska is the only remaining Senate election to be called. In that state, Democratic nominee Mary Peltola, a former House member, has a narrow lead over Sen. Dan Sullivan, the Republican incumbent.
"Blue Mississippi is here," Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., said in a post on X.
"Scott Colom is the only person who could've gotten this done. I knew it from the moment I met him," Schumer wrote.
In addition to the Senate, Democrats have won more than enough seats to take control of the House of Representatives when the next Congress begins in January.

articles.title: Nasdaq-100 futures slide, dragged lower as Nvidia sell-off resumes: Live updates
articles.text:
Nasdaq-100 futures fell Wednesday evening as Nvidia shares slid on a report that the chip giant's board is preparing to unseat CEO Jensen Huang.
Futures tied to the tech-heavy Nasdaq-100 lost 0.8%, while S&P 500 futures fell 0.4%. Dow Jones Industrial Average futures were little changed.
Japan's Nikkei 225 was slightly higher in choppy trading Thursday. South Korea's Kospi, which is dominated by Nvidia suppliers Samsung and SK Hynix, fell 0.35%. Hong Kong's Hang Seng index index fell 1.03% while China's CSI 300 was little changed. Australia's S&P/ASX 200 declined 0.31%.
In extended U.S. trading, selling resumed in Nvidia after The New York Times reported that Huang had an extramarital relationship with an executive at the company. The Wall Street Journal also reported that Nvidia's board is gearing up to remove Huang from his post. Shares were last down around 8%.
In regular trading, the Dow rose nearly 255 points, or 0.5%. The S&P 500 advanced 1.3%, and the Nasdaq Composite jumped 1.6%. The gains were driven by a post-earnings advance in CoreWeave and a rebound in Nvidia.
Investors are weighing whether the artificial intelligence-driven rally has more room to run given recent weakness in Nvidia, while CoreWeave's better-than-expected results and raised revenue outlook reinforced the longer-term growth story heading into Thursday's session.
AI enthusiasm may be driving markets, with added momentum from Anthropic's upcoming IPO. However, macro and policy risks argue for staying selective rather than chasing performance, according to Sameer Samana, head of global equities and real assets at Wells Fargo Investment Institute.
"We would be a little circumspect about the bounce-back as there are some things changing at the margin [like] stubborn inflation, more fed rate hikes, higher long-term interest rates, change in configuration in Washington DC [and] AI/data center regulation demands," he said.
Callie Cox, director of investment strategy at Plancorp, said that the tension between AI optimism and macroeconomic concerns could continue to weigh on sentiment.
"Lately, the stock market has been locked in a fierce battle between the hope of AI and the fear around interest rates and inflation," she said. "There doesn't seem to be much in between, and something may have to give."
Investors are now looking to upcoming economic data for further clues on inflation, the labor market and the broader outlook. On Thursday, the market will get initial jobless claims data at 8:30 a.m. ET, followed by existing home sales at 10 a.m.

articles.title: Nvidia prepares to oust Jensen Huang, WSJ reports — stock sinks
articles.text:
Shares of Nvidia fell more than 9% in after-hours trading on Wednesday after The Wall Street Journal reported that the company's board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang.
The news landed minutes after The New York Times reported that Huang had an extramarital relationship with another executive at the company. Nvidia's board is preparing to meet as soon as Wednesday to determine Huang's future at the company, according to the Journal.
The alleged relationship was with Kimberly Powell, vice president of health care at Nvidia, according to the Times' report. Powell's bio on the Nvidia website says she's "responsible for the company's worldwide healthcare business, including hardware and software platforms for accelerated computing, AI, and visualization that power the ecosystem of medical imaging, life sciences, drug discovery, and healthcare analytics."
Huang and Powell were reportedly captured on camera being affectionate with one another at a hotel in San Jose, California in March, according to the Times.
Nvidia and Powell did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment. Heller, the crisis PR firm Huang reportedly hired as early as last year, did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment.
The report comes days after Huang admitted to an affair with a woman who is believed by U.S. intelligence of being a Chinese spy. The CEO was romantically involved with Alice Huang, according to The Financial Times, who U.S. intelligence officials believe is a spy for China's Ministry of State Security, The New York Times reported.
Nvidia's board of directors has opened an independent investigation and hired the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to look into the spying allegations.
"I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did," Huang wrote in the message to Nvidia staff on Sunday. "I am deeply sorry."
Most of Huang's Nvidia shares are co-owned with his wife, Lori Huang, and are held in trusts. About 800 million shares are held by those trusts. Huang holds about 70 million shares on his own and has limited economic control over the company.
Rumors of an affair between Huang and Powell have circulated for years, in part because Powell lacks a background in health or science, according to a former employee who asked not to be named because of the sensitivity of the matter.
Healthcare is a smaller business at Nvidia. The company makes chips for medical devices and MRI machines, but they are a minor in comparison to the revenue generated from its advanced AI systems and graphics processing units, or GPUs. In recent appearances, including at the company's annual GTC conference, Powell has spoken about how Nvidia's AI technology can help accelerate drug discovery, assist providers and improve clinical efficiency. Powell has been leading the group since 2017.
Nvidia's stock was down 7% this week prior to the after-hours drop on Wednesday and is on pace for its sixth straight weekly slide, reflecting broad concern on the sustainability of the artificial intelligence buildout. The AI infrastructure trade was hit particularly hard last week after the midterm elections, as Democrats won sweeping majorities in both houses of Congress, and dozens of ballot measures past that could make building data centers more difficult.
Huang has become synonymous with the AI industry, and he is often referred to by his first name ,"Jensen," by customers and rivals. Nvidia has been one of the primary beneficiaries of the AI boom since its chips are used to train models and run large AI workloads.
—CNBC's Lora Kolodny and Kif Leswing contributed to this report

articles.title: Jensen Huang affair in D.C.: Resignation calls and moves to tighten Nvidia China exports
articles.text:
Members of Congress are calling on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to resign, and momentum is building to subpoena the executive, whose company is a leader in advanced artificial intelligence chips.
Senate banking committee member Kevin Cramer, R-N.D., doubled down Wednesday on his call for Huang to resign, and a key Democratic House oversight panel member and House Republican piled on.
"As a matter of his own conscience, he should resign," Cramer told CNBC, in response to revelations that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy as the chipmaker he co-founded was given permission from the U.S. government to sell its technology to China.
Huang, who leads a company that's been a chief beneficiary of the artificial intelligence boom, on Sunday admitted to having an affair with a woman whom news outlets have reported U.S. intelligence concluded was a Chinese spy. The revelation is sending shockwaves through Washington, with lawmakers now fearing that U.S. AI dominance could be at risk.
"What bothers me at the end of it is what we don't know is what she knows about him that can be utilized," Cramer said, referring to Alice Huang and Jensen Huang, who are not related. "This is a guy that's right now so vulnerable to extortion, blackmail. I just don't think, as a national security matter, we can run the risk."
Cramer's comments come on the deadline set by a trio of House lawmakers who requested Huang to testify before their committees on Nov. 18.
Subpoena power
GOP Reps. Brian Mast, chair of the House Foreign Affairs Committee; John Moolenaar, chair of the Permanent Select Committee on China; and Rick Crawford, who leads the House intelligence panel, called for Huang to appear in a Nov. 4 letter. Congress members in the majority party also have subpoena power, should they choose to use it.
Mast and Moolenaar told reporters on Wednesday afternoon that they had not yet heard from Huang and that they were giving him until the end of the day to respond.
Asked whether the committees were considering subpoenaing Huang if he doesn't agree to appear, Mast said "yes."
Moolenaar, when asked the same question, said "all three committees have subpoena power, and I know all three committees have a very serious interest in getting to the bottom of this and having transparency around this."
"We are going to continue to pursue this," Moolenaar said.
The lawmakers are far from alone in their criticism, concern and outright shock over the affair. And the scrutiny is only expected to intensify with Democrats poised to take over both chambers of Congress in January. Huang has been close with President Donald Trump during the president's second term, traveling on Air Force One to China in May.
"Jensen Huang should resign from Nvidia," Rep. Suhas Subramanyam, D-Va., a member of the House Oversight Committee, told CNBC. Subramanyam is the top Democrat on the panel's Subcommittee on Military and Foreign Affairs.
"I didn't agree with his sentiment that there's no downside to exporting chips to China," he said. "But I never thought that he might be having an affair with a Chinese spy who was helping smuggle chips into China at an alarming rate."
Rep. Don Bacon, R-Neb., who is retiring from Congress after sometimes bucking Trump, also said the CEO should step down.
"From the little I know, yes." Bacon told CNBC in response to whether Huang should resign. "I mean, he allowed himself to get compromised by the Chinese government. Not good."
Export controls
Huang was notably opposed to strict export controls on AI chips to China, which ruffled feathers with China hawks on Capitol Hill.
Democrats are widely expected to launch myriad investigations into the White House and industry when they assume control of both chambers of Congress in January. Nvidia is now likely to be at the center of those probes.
"There's two parts to this investigation that [need] to happen somewhere immediately," Subramanyam said. "One is what was going on with Nvidia and China, and two is why the administration did nothing about it even though they appeared to have known, and what the administration knew, and what influence the money from Nvidia and Jensen Huang had on this administration, essentially staying silent."
Rep. Jay Obernolte, R-Calif., co-chair of the House AI task force, said Tuesday he hopes that the Huang scandal can avoid becoming a distraction in talks about imposing export controls on advanced AI chips.
The situation may give Congress additional ammunition as it tries to pass a suite of bills in this year's National Defense Authorization Act to tighten export controls on advanced AI chips.
Congress has still not passed the annual defense bill, which is a top priority for lawmakers in the lame-duck session.
Those bills include the AI Overwatch Act, the MATCH Act and the Chip Security Act — all of which are aimed at preventing U.S. chip technology from falling into adversarial hands.
Sens. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., and Jim Banks, R-Ind., in a statement following the revelation of Huang's affair, urged their colleagues to include the AI Overwatch Act. Warren, the incoming Senate banking committee chair, sponsored the bill in the Senate with Banks.
"Huang's confirmation of a relationship with a suspected spy for China's intelligence service makes these national security concerns even more urgent and raises important questions NVIDIA must answer about the extent to which these activities were related," the senators said. "It is time for Congress to take decisive action to pass key bills like the AI Overwatch Act in the NDAA that will cut off pathways through which China accesses advanced chips."
And Subramanyam warned that what Nvidia does now — and whether Huang remains atop the company — could affect its relationship with Washington and whether lawmakers crack down.
"If Nvidia finds out that he knew about what was going on and does nothing about it, then Nvidia is making a choice and us as regulators and as watchdogs need to defend the American people," he said.

articles.title: Feds arrest top official of healthcare company, alleging illegal drug importation
articles.text:
U.S. authorities are accusing the two top officials of a Canadian company of operating a long-running scheme to illegally import prescription drugs into the U.S., according to court records filed Tuesday.
John Thomas Howard, treasurer and a director of the company, CANARX, was arrested Sunday on smuggling and conspiracy charges, according to the records.
Bob Howard, his brother, who is president and a director of CANARX, is also wanted in the federal investigation, according to an affidavit from Dustin Dobbs, a special agent with the Food and Drug Administration's Office of Criminal Investigations. He has not yet been taken into custody.
Besides conspiracy and smuggling, the arrest warrant said John Thomas Howard was charged with introducing misbranded drugs into interstate commerce and illegal drug importation. No plea has been filed.
CANARX was featured in a CNBC investigation last year that revealed how the company and others known as alternative funding programs, or AFPs, are becoming more pervasive around the U.S. as drug costs skyrocket. The investigation found these companies have penetrated the country's healthcare system by offering high-cost specialty drugs at more affordable prices through private and public employers. In some cases, employers are requiring their staff to use an AFP.
AFPs often obtain the medications overseas and ship them directly to patients, a practice that federal authorities have said is illegal and poses safety risks. CNBC traced the trail of drugs from abroad to the U.S. via a supply chain that the pharmaceutical companies producing the medications have not authorized.
On its website, CANARX, founded in 2002 and based in Windsor, Ontario, Canada, described its business as the first international prescription provider for the U.S. and the safest such program in the industry. The company said it sources its medications from Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia and New Zealand.
But the affidavit said that the FDA's investigation found "there is probable cause to believe that (CANARX) illegally imported or caused the illegal importation of prescription drugs into the United States …."
The affidavit does not specify which medications the agency believes were illegally imported. The criminal complaint covers the period from Feb. 22, 2017, through April 15, 2026.
The company's general counsel, Joseph Morris, told CNBC in a statement: "The Howards deny all the charges against them, will defend vigorously, and expect to be vindicated in court."
The company has been under FDA scrutiny for several years. In 2023, the agency seized medication being shipped by CANARX that it says was potentially misbranded and counterfeit, according to an email sent to a patient that was obtained by CNBC.
And in 2019, the FDA sent a warning letter to the company, saying it was operating "in a manner that substitutes the FDA-approved drugs prescribed by the U.S. healthcare provider with unapproved drugs." Morris, in response to that warning, argued CANARX was not misleading patients, but agreed for the company to stop importing drugs that need to be administered by a doctor.
In an interview as part of the CNBC investigation, Morris said last year that the medicines shipped to U.S. patients come from highly regulated countries. He said CANARX was operating legally.
The central question for AFPs is the legality of importing prescription drugs into the U.S. for personal use. The FDA allows Americans to import medications for individual use in some cases if the drug is not available domestically. That is the basis on which the AFPs built their models for shipping medicines directly to patients.
But an FDA spokesperson told CNBC last year that "in most circumstances, a person cannot import prescription drugs from other countries into the U.S. ... as substitutes for FDA-approved drugs."
In a separate civil lawsuit that is pending, Gilead Sciences accused CANARX and other companies of illegally importing Biktarvy, its medication to treat HIV.
In a statement to CNBC on Wednesday, a Gilead spokesperson said the company "has taken strong legal action to protect patients and the integrity of the U.S. medicines supply chain. We welcome the government's efforts to hold accountable those whose conduct may put patients at risk."
CANARX has not responded to the Gilead lawsuit.
— CNBC's Paige Tortorelli and Melissa Lee contributed to this report

articles.title: Costco is giving shareholders a big, early holiday gift. How to make sure you get it
articles.text: Costco is rewarding shareholders with a big payout ahead of the holidays, and it's not too late to get in on the action. For the sixth time in company history, the retailer is offering a special dividend. To get the $30-a-share payout, announced Tuesday evening , investors must be shareholders of record by the close of business on Nov. 24. (Typically, that means you need to own the stock one business day prior.) It will be payable on Dec. 4. Costco also announced a $4 billion stock buyback plan, which is another way to return capital to shareholders because fewer shares outstanding means a higher ownership percentage in the company without having to purchase more stock. Jim Cramer praised the moves. On "Mad Money" after the announcement, he said, "Shame on those of us who, for a moment, thought maybe Costco was overvalued." He added, "Glad that my Charitable Trust stuck with it. It's a buy." Before the opening bell, Jim said the stock should soon go back to record highs. It almost did Wednesday morning — rallying to a few dollars shy of its all-time high of $1,096 on May 19 before paring some of those gains. COST YTD mountain Costco YTD Earlier this month, after strong October sales, we documented the rise in Costco stock as the market has recently been rotating out of the AI trade and into consumer staple stocks like Costco and other defensive names. Quarter-to-date, Costco stock has soared more than 18%, bringing its year-to-date gains to 25%. For comparison, the S & P 500 is up 11.5% in 2026. If recent history is any guide, the five other special dividends issued by Costco, dating back to November 2012, have been good for an average stock gain of 1.5% for the roughly two-week period from the announcement day to the record date. The one announced on Dec. 14, 2023, was good for a 5% pop in the stock by the record date. That was the best stock performance of the bunch. On the flip side, the one announced on Nov. 28, 2012 resulted in a 4.9% decline in the stock by the record date. That was the worst. To be sure, those stock moves are a function of only looking at the charts, without taking into account other factors that may or may not have influenced the share prices during those time periods. Deutsche Bank also sees Costco's latest payout as another reason to justify the stock's high price-to-earnings ratio of 46.4 times next 12 months' earnings estimates. The S & P 500's forward P/E is less than half that. "While special dividends remain discretionary and do not change our underlying earnings outlook, we believe the increasing size of these distributions ... provides another tangible proof point supporting Costco's premium valuation," the analysts wrote Tuesday evening. As veteran investors in Costco, we are not strangers to premium valuation. But time and time again, the stock has proven it is worth it, handily outperforming the S & P 500 over the long haul. Shares more than doubled over five years; soared more than 600% over the past decade; and skyrocketed over 1,930% over the past 20 years. Costco's appeal goes beyond its shareholder rewards. Jim praised the company's efforts to keep prices down for consumers battling the elevated costs of everyday items from groceries to gasoline. October's hotter-than-expected consumer price index Tuesday served as a reminder of those pressures. "It's all pricing. It's all pricing. Remember, they want pricing low because they're making all the money on the [membership] card," Jim said. "This is about how you have a plan to help America save money, and it works." One way Costco has managed to keep prices competitive is through its popular Kirkland Signature private-label brand. Jim pointed to Costco's Kirkland Vodka as an example of how the company has challenged established brands like Tito's by offering a similar product at a better price. As of Wednesday, a check of Costco's website with a New York City zip code showed that a 1.75-liter bottle of Tito's costs around $30, compared with a little over $13 for the Kirkland brand. The other side of what makes Costco stellar, as Jim has regularly pointed out, is Costco's membership-based business model. Instead of relying solely on profits from individual product sales, Costco generates a significant portion of its income through annual membership fees. While reporting sales on a monthly basis, which keeps the mystery out of the top-line number, Costco only reports its membership numbers quarterly. Membership trends, which have shown slowing growth and wobbly renewal rates, will be the big watch item when Costco reports the first quarter of its new 2027 fiscal year, or the November quarter. The membership metrics in the company's fiscal fourth quarter ended in August were OK but nothing to write home about. (Jim Cramer's Charitable Trust is long COST. articles.title: Insiders are starting to buy this retail turnaround story, so I am too
articles.text: Dick's Sporting Goods shares are starting to climb back out of the abyss they fell into over the summer after the leading sports retailer lowered guidance. Now that corporate insiders are starting to buy in, I believe the turnaround has some legs. Dick's bucked the 2020 Covid hit on brick-and-mortar retailers and delivered amazing shareholder returns the subsequent next four years, with the stock even doubling in 2021 alone. Things started to go wrong when it purchased troubled Foot Locker for more than $2 billion in 2025. The shares dropped 13% in 2025. This year the struggles continued, including a 30% tumble in a single day this August after Dick's cut its EPS forecast for the year because of the sales underperformance by Foot Locker stores. Higher gasoline prices haven't helped either. The stock is recovering now, with the shares up nearly 25% from their low — and I believe the comeback can continue. Here's why: Key points The company is making progress on turning around Foot Locker. Corporate insiders are buying shares in large amounts with some board directors making their first purchases in years. The core Dick's stores are working, taking market share and introducing new concepts. Why I'm buying Foot Locker unit is improving Dick's is making progress with Foot Locker by clearing old inventory and launching new products. Competitor On Holding AG had a recent analyst day where the shoe seller said it saw a meaningful pick-up in U.S. wholesale sales, which I believe bodes well for Foot Locker sales. Insiders are buying Six insiders purchased Dick's shares in the 30 days following the August drop in the stock, totaling $5.1 million at around $130 a share, according to Verity Research. The third quarter saw the largest insider buying activity seen in the stock in more than a decade, per Verity. CFO Navdeep Gupta was a buyer after showing a consistent pattern of selling over the years. This shows me that the insiders have confidence that the stock is cheap and that the turnaround is happening at Foot Locker. Core Dick's is doing well Core Dick's is about 75% of total revenue, and it's actually doing pretty well with quarterly comparable same-store sales running at 4%-to-5%. They've actually gained market share in the last six years to 9% from 7% overall. Dick's is driving traffic to stores by making them destinations with batting cages, ice rinks and climbing walls. Its loyalty program has led to 30 million members. Why now? DKS YTD mountain Dick's, YTD The stock trades at less than 12 times forward earnings, below its 10-year average of 14. Shares also sport a 3.3% dividend yield, a hefty payout compared to other retailers which allows you to generate some income while the turnaround unfolds. Bottom line The turnaround is underway at Dick's and I think the valuation is very compelling — and apparently so do executives.
